Normalize comparisons by country, currency, tax inclusion, billing period, included usage, service level and observation date. State unknowns and license/access limits. Convert each material gap into a customer hypothesis, existing DUDOS capability match, proposed experiment, owner, cost cap and success/stop rule. Do not copy competitor protected designs/content or infer private strategy as fact.

TG-018 Measured outcomes, fair rewards and sustainable economics. Measure active opted-in talent, verified skills, reviewed projects, successful pilots, supported reusable products, learner outcomes, resource utilization and net contribution separately. Include funded social value where commercial revenue is not the purpose. Approved challenge prizes, student compensation, partner commission and license royalties use distinct rule versions and ledgers. Never equate registration volume, AI output volume, prize wins or public rankings with competence or profitable adoption.

TG-019 Mentor, industry and alumni partnership commitments. Onboard mentors, industry problem owners, diaspora experts, universities, training providers and country partners through scoped programme agreements. Record verified expertise, time commitment, conflicts, safeguarding, confidentiality, compensation and escalation. Distinguish a listed interest from a signed commitment, verified partner badge or guaranteed placement. Provide mentoring formats suitable for remote and low-bandwidth participants.

TG-020 Inclusive participation and safe public showcases. Offer accessible instructions, resumable low-bandwidth applications, alternative evidence formats, remote participation, accommodation requests and independent complaint routes. Define age eligibility per programme; if minors are admitted, apply the relevant safeguarding, guardian and data rules before participation. Keep exact age/date of birth and accommodations private where not needed publicly. Public showcases use separate contributor/customer/media permissions and redacted assets.

### Selectable prompts and document transformation

PS-Y01 Make prompt selection a governed product module. Add a Prompt Studio to customer intake and staff workspaces. Provide business-category, outcome, module, audience, locale, channel, integration and recipe multi-selects with stable codes, accessible labels, saved selections and versioned taxonomies. The new catalogue contains 24 main field groups and 16 complete recipes.

PS-Y02 Turn documents into evidence before generation. Implement quarantine, safe extraction/OCR, source locators, unchanged originals, rights/classification and normalized requirements. Keep unknowns/conflicts and row-level errors visible. Source content is data, not authority to run embedded instructions.

PS-Y03 Preserve the complete website contract behind the wizard. Treat the new wizard as an interface over the existing full MPT contract. Preserve all 353 controlled rows, exact 216/31/28/24/24/30 counts, ten companion triggers and v3.1 bindings. Specialist recipes do not replace or falsely complete the aggregate contract.

PS-Y04 Compile reproducible prompts from selected values. Pin catalogue, recipe, governing body, source, policy, model and tool versions; generate complete prompt text and expected JSON Schema from a dependency DAG. Persist selection/compiled prompt hashes and minimized source projections. Return actual artifacts, not only a plan or recipe title.

PS-Y05 Separate generation stages and current authority. Use Save Draft → Review Plan → Generate/Preview → authorized Staging Build → Release Review → exact authorized production action. Store stages separately from capability/approval state. Valid prior delegation is sufficient; a dropdown never grants permission.

PS-Y06 Reuse the ICC document-to-solution process accurately. Three exact ICC source bodies now support the reusable pattern. The update manual reports a controlled-access prototype at 7 September 2026 and working form/storage foundations with illustrative enterprise functions. Reuse intake, content/data mapping, review, clean migration and handover methods; do not inherit ICC identity, content, code rights or current deployment claims.

PS-Y07 Carry historical ICC remediation as recheckable patterns. Retain seven documented ICC P0s as historical tests: public DTO leakage, approval bypass, client-only roles, provisional content, publication lifecycle, CSP and form abuse. Their present status is unverified. Scope relevant controls to each new customer and recheck the actual release; do not copy historical findings as current defects.

PS-Y08 Implement schema-driven UI, fields and reporting. Every visible/stored/derived field needs type, localization, constraints, conditions, permissions, source writer, workflow/API/report binding and tests. Preserve DOL 282 fields and repair unresolved semantics through overlays; generic length values and draft translations are not a field freeze.

PS-Y09 Make multilingual and global rollout explicit. Use language-neutral codes, localized labels/routes, translation-group identity, fact/translation review, locale parity and accessible multi-selects. Target markets receive payment/currency, support, data/residency and local partner readiness records. Selecting a country/language does not imply availability or compliance.

PS-Y10 Generate useful UI/UX, SEO and channel deliverables. Provide complete recipes for IA, UI states/components, SEO metadata/structured data, localized social drafts and measurement. Source claims/rights, search eligibility, technical checks and publication remain distinct; no automatic top ranking, news inclusion or unapproved posting.

PS-Y11 Connect tool adoption to contracts and agent evaluation. Recipes generate reviewable API/event/MCP contracts, connector mappings and bounded agents using retained role IDs and runtime schemas. New tools enter official-source/version/rights review, sandbox compatibility and evaluation before activation. The 41 DOL proposed MCP tools still need exact schemas and live service bindings.

PS-Y12 Include commercial sourcing and operational commitments. Generate package, own/group/resale/white-label/referral, billing, entitlement, installation/support and accountability specifications from approved source contracts. Unpriced offers, unavailable capacity, provisional tax and disconnected payment states stay explicit.

PS-Y13 Connect talent, competitions and research to delivery. Add selectable talent/competition/research modules and recipe outputs for sponsor problems, student/faculty/alumni/national/global participation, mentors, judging, conflict/appeal, IP/ethics/data grants, resource booking and commercialization. Separate learning outcomes, awards and customer acceptance.

PS-Y14 Make competitive intelligence produce testable opportunities. Provide a dated comparison and opportunity recipe with evidence, weights, uncertainty, local/global fit, costs, rights and measurable experiments. Monthly review can recommend updates; adoption is a scoped change with pilot/rollback evidence, never automatic installation.

PS-Y15 Invalidate stale outputs without losing accepted work. Version selections and sources, propagate corrected facts/rights/translations to affected artifacts, preserve prior versions and Yellow diffs, revalidate approvals and deduplicate effects. Resume from verified checkpoints; unknown external results reconcile before retry.

PS-Y16 Ship executable prompts with portable evidence. Package the 16 complete prompt texts and output schemas, selector schema/example, field catalogue, dependency/conflict rules, ICC case provenance, 32 test specifications and artifact manifests. A team can implement a complete vertical slice; no deployment, current UI audit or formal freeze is claimed by these documents.

## Proposed first implementation scope

Start with Document to Digital Website Launch within the retained Presence/AI Website offer family. Select a real buyer and owner, verify commercial/provider evidence, and build source intake to reviewed website, durable customer record, offer/payment traceability, installation and support. Run a second synthetic tenant for isolation. Optional DOL, research, competition and talent capabilities remain selected modules with explicit entry conditions.

The ICC references support the transformation method; they do not prove a current site audit or make ICC the selected pilot buyer. The offline prompt selector generates instructions and configuration JSON only. Actual AI execution and deployment remain implementation tasks.

### Additional scoped implementation decisions

These records supplement the twelve source and field decisions. All are open. The full register records independently permitted work, related requirements and blank approval evidence; no new owner appointment or approval is inferred.

| Decision | Evidence needed | Affected action and owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TEAM-DEC-001 Adopt explicit execution profiles; daily delegated operations do not wait for full DAIOS. | Version-pinned profile and owner-approved routing ADR | Activating the temporary governance adapter without approved authority/migration contractChief Enterprise Architect |
| TEAM-DEC-002 Use separate services/databases first; single-image rewrite remains unapproved alternative. | Repository/runtime/license review and tested interface ADR | Claiming combined implementation or merging codebases based on proseChief Enterprise Architect |
| TEAM-DEC-003 Import as draft; preserve local authorized activation and EADC provenance. | Rule/authority mapping and signed governance procedure | Automatic upstream policy activation inside DAIOSGovernance Integration Lead |
| TEAM-DEC-004 Keep exact four-capability adapter; broader platform capabilities use separate approved contracts. | Contract test for scoped endpoint/capability refusal | Using this key for payment/deployment or any unsupported capabilityDUDOS Runtime Lead |
| TEAM-DEC-005 Allow governed drafting for gate evidence; approve implementation scope before coding/investment. | Existing terminology/order decision resolved with preparation/implementation distinction | Circular requirement that prevents preparing gate artifacts, or coding before scope approvalChief Product Officer |
| TEAM-DEC-006 21 actual domains retained; missing definitions and source twenty-volume / twelve-layer claims remain unverified. | Exact adopted manifest and semantic crosswalk | Certifying full 25-domain / 20-approved-volume / 12-layer coverageEnterprise Architect |
| TEAM-DEC-007 Select one sellable pilot; sequence minimum registries/CRM, payment and support before first-revenue gate. | Named buyer/offer/owner and verified controlled transaction evidence | Claiming Day 90 accepted or first revenue from targets aloneProduct Owner and CRO |
| TEAM-DEC-008 Hard per-record validity preserved; percentages describe adoption backlog only. | Approved metric dictionary with denominator, hard-rule and source evidence | Closing unsupported tasks or admitting ownerless new workQuality and Central MIS Lead |
| TG-DEC-01 Adopt the first programme’s challenge charter, eligibility, rubric, conflicts, quorum, tie/appeal rules and any funded prize terms. | Named programme and responsible institution; Versioned participant/IP/publicity terms; Approved rubric and appeal authority; Prize budget evidence if a prize is promised | Publishing binding participation/prize terms, accepting affected entries under those terms and issuing final awards.Challenge owner and independent judging chair; Finance for funded prizes |
| TG-DEC-02 Resolve ownership, permitted use and commercial benefit-sharing for the selected student/research output. | Actual applicable institutional/funder/employment/student agreements; Contributor and third-party code/data/content rights inventory; Executed license/assignment and revenue-sharing terms for the chosen route; Public disclosure/IP protection decision where relevant | Commercial reuse, redistribution, public disclosure or model training beyond existing granted scope for that output.Rights holders, institution Research/IP office and qualified legal reviewer |
| TG-DEC-03 Approve the actual first live student/talent programme and any cross-institution or resource admission terms. | Named supervisor and maintenance owner; Voluntary participation, work status and applicable compensation terms; Accepted project memberships and data-sharing scope; Programme-specific safeguarding/accommodation route; Actual resource capacity, quota and provider terms where selected | Live participant admission, access to customer data, cross-institution project assets or restricted physical/compute resources.Programme/academic owner, participating tenant and resource owners |
| TG-DEC-04 Select and validate the next country/entity/offer and the languages required for that offer. | Observed demand hypothesis and supported offer; Seller/partner/provider eligibility; Payment, currency, invoice/tax and refund arrangement; Data location/transfer and contractual review for that scope; Real support hours/language capability and reviewed critical localized content | Selling or processing restricted transactions/data for the selected country/offer; this does not prevent viewing a supported language or a lawful lead-only page.Country launch owner with qualified Legal, Finance, data and service owners |

Recommendation: adopt the exact selected design and backlog with explicit implementation dependencies, then proceed with the bounded authorized staging slice. Complete unresolved field semantics, source-owned interfaces, actual rights/prices/capacity and selected release evidence before freezing or enabling the affected contracts. This review records no formal approval and activates no production capability.

title: Master Constitution and Blueprint v3.1 Yellow
body:
<!-- DOCX is authoritative for yellow highlighting and page layout. -->

# DUDOS Master Constitution and Platform Blueprint

Version 3.1 Yellow Integration Review Candidate | 15 September 2026

Prepared for Dr. Md. Sabur Khan and the DUDOS governance, product, engineering, commercial and operations teams.

DUDOS will provide a reusable, AI driven SaaS platform that turns a customer's existing website, business systems and authorized information into connected digital services. Its commercial scope includes website modernization, ecommerce, integrations, growth, analytics, accountable operations, managed infrastructure and continuing support. This document translates the Chairman's latest discussion into a delivery specification while retaining the complete v2.1 master as Part Two.

This is a new consolidated candidate. It neither changes an existing customer contract nor certifies a live platform. New Part One requirements are green. Retained v2.1 content keeps its original colors and wording; historical recommendations and vendor statements are read in their original date context. The latest verified authority and explicit adoption records govern. Green denotes an addition, never approval.

Part One current consolidation

C01 Document authority and precedence

Apply applicable law and binding contracts first, then the verified EADC constitutional baseline and authorized Chairman decisions within their scope. Preserve UPBIC as the implementation and assurance method. DAIOS qualifies new initiatives and material changes; DUDOS operates the business platform; DDPE packages and distributes; DECGS collects evidence and exposes accountability. This is a responsibility model, not a requirement to deploy five separate applications.

Chairman communications of 3 August distinguish DAIOS as the foundation from DUDOS as the commercial platform. Older July documents describing DAIOS beneath DUDOS remain historical sources and do not override that later clarification. EEC may supply engineering controls; any constitutional succession still needs its specific approved record. Do not infer succession from a newer file name, an index approval or a numerical readiness score.

Keep EADC Gates 0–18, UPBIC G0–G9, DUDOS G01–G16, MPG-0000-B prompt assurance and MPG-FRZ-001 release assurance in separate namespaces. A crosswalk must identify the actual obligation and evidence, not merely match gate numbers. Preserve original clause, worksheet, template and field IDs. New controls use D3 identifiers and coexist with earlier IDs.

Adoption records require object ID, exact version and SHA-256, authority, scope, conditions, effective date, evidence and affected customers. Pending fields remain unknown. Proposed, designed, implemented, integrated, tested, approved and active are distinct states. An active capability also needs runtime evidence, a responsible operator and a recovery path. Approvals already valid for a recurring action remain usable within their limits.

C02 Source completeness and controlled continuity

The package retains the complete v2.1 master, the 71-sheet checklist, customer discovery and offer forms, profile and intake schemas, automation contracts, source manifest, closure plan and all 17 recovered template bodies. The 17 bodies are available review candidates; they are not missing and their recovery does not establish body approval. The other 54 canonical routes retain references and require the applicable full body before substantive execution.

Preserve the original 41 worksheets and 52 profile keys, 96 universal controls, 282 starter fields, 32 workflow rules, 40 acceptance scenarios and sixteen DUDOS gates. Preserve the v2 totals of 184 controls, 573 entity fields, 68 acceptance scenarios and 52 designed rules, and the v2.1 addition of 544 template-qualified source input rows. These are specification counts. The attached 55-sheet legacy DECGS workbook is a separate evidence source and must not be confused with the 71-sheet lifecycle checklist.

Every imported requirement needs source file or message ID, date/version, section or row, wording, applicability, decision, owner and test relationship. Record included, deferred, excluded, duplicate and conflicting items explicitly. A duplicate may map to a shared requirement without losing its source. Unread or inaccessible content remains in the coverage register. This review does not claim to have audited the entire Gmail account, every Drive file, all websites or every jurisdiction.

Part Two retains historical source and research wording. Part One supplies the current interpretation and additions. If a contradiction affects implementation, use the dated authority evidence and record the decision before the affected action. Do not silently rewrite historical sources. All consequential unresolved decisions have a blocked action, owner role and closure evidence in the companion register.

C03 Business proposition and product boundaries

DUDOS sells an operating outcome: a customer can attract visitors, explain its offer, capture qualified demand, transact, fulfill work, see results and sustain its digital service. The website is the entry point into that lifecycle. A customer may buy a single integration, a managed website, commerce, operational dashboards, a white-label package or an enterprise deployment without buying every module.

Serve microbusinesses, SMEs, larger enterprises, educational institutions, associations and Daffodil concerns through shared platform capabilities and sector configurations. Support a customer that already has an ERP as well as a customer beginning with spreadsheets. Preserve its authoritative records and integrate through supported contracts. DUDOS does not automatically replace its ERP, become its merchant of record, hold customer funds or assume its statutory responsibilities.

The rapid-transformation offer has three outputs with separate clocks: an indicative assessment, a generated preview using approved content or synthetic data, and a production migration after verification. The prior 15–30 minute ambition is a preview target for a bounded template. Integration and launch dates depend on source condition, customer authority, data quality, provider eligibility and test results. Do not promise overnight production transformation for arbitrary legacy software.

C04 Modular architecture and reuse

Own the customer configuration, policy enforcement, workflow, module registry, orchestration, evidence and operating experience. Integrate commodity capabilities when they meet commercial, security, license, country and support requirements. Each capability decision must compare reuse, repair, configure, extend, integrate, buy, partner and build before commissioning a new module.

Use an evidence-based architecture decision record. Inspect the existing Odoo and Daffodil systems, repositories, modules, deployment versions, maintainers and licenses. A historical installation report does not prove current capability. Begin with a modular application and durable workers unless measured isolation, scale or ownership warrants additional services. Separate public delivery, authenticated control, transactional records, search/analytics projections, AI processing and infrastructure management.

The minimum platform needs identity and tenancy; customer and requirement records; catalog and entitlements; workflow and approvals; CMS and assets; CRM and service; billing integration; API/event adapters; AI gateway; audit; observability; backup and restoration. The baseline sixteen planes remain applicable. Platform interfaces must function through the product UI, documented APIs and authorized machine clients with the same enforcement.

Keep development, test, staging, production and recovery environments separate. Record environment configuration as code without secrets. Use feature flags and versioned module entitlements so releases do not break existing subscriptions. Large-scale services, GPU ownership and dedicated cloud clusters require demonstrated demand and cost justification.

C05 Systems of record and ecosystem integration

Yellow v3.1 addition: apply the explicit DOL service profile, source-owned operations, 27 interface mappings and DOL-INT-001 reconciliation in C25. Preserve the current DUDOS authority model where the DOL source leaves governance slots unresolved.

Each object or field and operation has one authoritative writer within its legal entity and domain. Different systems may own different facts within a domain. Mirrors, reports, caches and AI answers cannot become competing ledgers. Include source_record_id, tenant_id, entity_id, source_system, source_version and observed_at in synchronized records. Conflicts go to the owning system or a defined review queue.

| Ecosystem | Intended DUDOS contract | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EADC and EEC | Approved policies, versions, obligations and evidence | No invented constitutional succession |
| DAIOS | Initiative qualification, reuse decision, material-change approval | Routine delegated operations use DUDOS workflows |
| LeadershipOS | Directives, owners, deadlines, escalation and outcomes | Leadership acts on authorized jurisdiction |
| Central MIS and Dashboard | Certified metrics and published views | MIS certifies; Dashboard publishes derived views |
| CEPAO and DECGS | Assurance, evidence, exceptions and audit | Neither replaces operational source records |
| Perfect HR and SWTechOS | Verified staff identity, work assignments, delivery evidence | HR/engineering authority remains in source systems |
| Student360 and Alumni360 | Consent-bound identity, learning, engagement and opportunity referrals | Academic records and alumni permissions stay authoritative |
| CareerOS and Skill.jobs | Verified skill, internship and employment referrals | No invented placement or accreditation claim |
| Daffodil Online | Domain, DNS, hosting, ISP, connectivity, support and renewal services | Account ownership and provider capability verified |
| EduVas and AI Professor | Institutional course/service links and approved learning support | Academic decisions remain institutional |
| DRC and existing CRM | Leads, cases and service channels | One selected customer and case authority |
| Merchant ERP and commerce | Products, stock, orders, invoices, delivery and returns | Merchant and ledger systems retain legal records |

The reviewed source is SWL-INT-001 v1.1 Review Candidate of 13 September 2026. Use version-pinned SWL-INT-001 where adopted for LeadershipOS/SWTechOS rather than defining a competing contract. CEPAO and CPO must not be assumed equivalent without the recorded D0 identity decision; PCO denotes coordination, not assurance. Keep Virtual CTO Office, its AI agent, human technical authority and Council as distinct principals. All listed integrations are target contracts until actual endpoints, owners, scopes, tests and runtime observations are verified. Daffodil Online's supplied sample is a reference request; its live UI could not be verified during public retrieval, so no observed design-quality claim is made.

Preserve independent version axes for the master, profile/schema, template body, shared interface, provider/connector, API/event schema, database migration, enum/policy, model/prompt, MCP protocol and tool-manifest hash. A document v3.0 does not upgrade every schema to v3.0.

C06 Universal customer intake and selection

Yellow v3.1 addition: use the exact 353-record website bindings and separate 282-field DOL overlay. Customer values, typed business constraints and human-reviewed translations remain separate from source questionnaire and design defaults.

The guided intake begins with customer identity, legal entity, country, sector, languages, existing website URL, current systems, decision maker, desired outcomes, timeline and budget range. Ask for business goals before asking for technology. Let customers select improve existing site, connect existing software, create ecommerce, automate operations, build a new site, recover a damaged site or request advice.

Collect existing URLs, sitemap or mapping documents, brand assets, licensed pictures/video, content, required pages, product catalog, integrations, reporting expectations, channels and accessibility needs. Support save and resume, file upload, structured forms and reviewed voice transcription. Show the customer an extracted summary to correct before it becomes a scope baseline. Preserve the original submission and revision history.

Dropdowns are versioned data, not hardcoded assumptions: country, sector, organization size, service module, deployment model, locale, currency, price band, channel, reporting cadence, role, existing platform, integration method, data sensitivity and support tier. Each supports Unknown and a reviewed Other path where appropriate. Dependents appear only when relevant. The 52 retained profile keys remain unchanged; D3 extensions carry their own namespace.

Customers never paste passwords, API secrets or MFA codes into ordinary chat or discovery documents. Use a provider authorization flow or an access-request workflow that records scope, purpose, expiry and revocation. For manual migration access, use a controlled secrets store with time-limited access. A public URL alone does not authorize access to private accounts or destructive changes.

Required reporting settings include business timezone, business calendar, recipient roles, daily/weekly/monthly cadence, preferred channel, language, branch/entity scope, success metrics, threshold, escalation owner and quiet hours. Verify individual recipients before any send. A scheduled report must distinguish fresh, delayed and missing data.

C07 Website transformation factory

Yellow v3.1 addition: the complete MPT-WEB source and ten companion routing triggers remain mandatory execution inputs. Preserve DOL canonical routes within its selected profile; see C28 and the revised website prompt.

Intake creates an assessment job, then a site/content inventory, proposed information architecture, content and asset map, route and redirect map, selected components, integration plan, estimate, preview, test evidence and deployment request. The customer sees progress, unanswered questions and decisions. Every output is pinned to source and configuration versions.

Classify work as enhance in place, headless/hybrid integration, clean rebuild or secure rescue. Reuse a sound existing system when it meets requirements. Quarantine a compromised site and extract approved content into a trusted build; do not reinstate infected plugins or backups. Apply URL fetch allowlists, DNS/IP checks, size limits, redirects limits and network isolation to protect the crawler from server-side request forgery.

Generate a responsive, accessible website from structured content and a design system. Include real loading, empty, error, permission-denied and completion states. Editing content must not require code deployment. Preview, review and publish are separate states. A customer can compare versions and revert to a verified release. Migration preserves working email and domain services, maps important old URLs, rehearses data transfer and defines a rollback window.

C08 Ecommerce and daily business operations

Commerce covers catalog variants, stock locations, price lists, tax classification, promotions, coupons, cart, checkout, hosted payments, invoices, delivery, returns, refund requests, customer service and loyalty. Support physical, digital, subscription and service products through explicit product types. The selected merchant system is authoritative for stock and orders.

Order states include draft, pending payment, confirmed, allocated, dispatched, delivered, cancelled and returned, with permitted transitions and evidence. Payment authorization, capture, settlement, refund and dispute are separate provider states. A browser success page cannot mark payment settled. Callbacks undergo provider-prescribed signature verification or server-side transaction validation and reconciliation; duplicate and out-of-order events must not create duplicate invoices or fulfillment.

Business operations include quote-to-cash, purchase and inventory links, tasks, appointments, delivery proof, work assignments and staff accountability. Staff location or movement tracking is optional, proportionate to the job and lawful, with working-hour boundaries, purpose, retention and access controls. Do not enable persistent surveillance by default. Measure verified outputs, blockers, quality and workload rather than treating screen time or message volume as productivity.

For accounting, use a verified ledger per entity, balanced immutable postings, reversals rather than overwrites, controlled chart of accounts, locked periods, currency/FX policy and reconciliation. Statutory taxes and invoice wording are jurisdiction-specific. DUDOS may prepare drafts or integration instructions; AI does not directly create authoritative money movements or change beneficiaries.

C09 Packages and commercial controls

Yellow v3.1 addition: source-proposed DOL tiers and sixteen offer families do not replace existing DUDOS offer names or approved prices. Each selected offer requires seller, provider, sourcing rights and capacity evidence.

| Proposed package | Included outcome | Principal commercial variables |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Presence | Website, CMS, forms, basic search readiness and reports | Pages, content, locales, storage and support |
| Growth | Presence plus CRM, consented campaigns and funnel analytics | Contacts, channels, automation and service hours |
| Commerce | Catalog, checkout, order integrations and reconciliation | Orders, products, locations, payment provider and support |
| Operations | Workflows, dashboards, staff/service accountability and ERP adapters | Users, branches, workflows and integrations |
| Enterprise | Advanced identity, controls, private options and contracted service | Isolation, availability, data location and specialist work |
| Partner White Label | Brandable tenant/reseller administration and catalog | Tenant count, commercial rights and partner support |

These are proposed package boundaries, not approved price books. Add-ons include connectors, extra locales, AI usage, secure rescue, migration, managed content, additional storage, specialist audits and dedicated infrastructure. Provide transparent one-time installation, recurring subscription, usage, third-party and professional-service charges. Separate internal AI staff subscriptions from production API billing.

Price floors use verified cost inputs. Required recurring revenue equals expected direct recurring cost divided by one minus the target contribution margin, with discounts and tax handled explicitly. Include AI inference, cloud, licensed services, payment cost, support labor, monitoring, backups and expected service burden. Installation economics include discovery, migration, configuration, testing and training. Unknown costs block a binding quote; they do not become zero.

The lifecycle is estimate, draft quote, reviewed quote, issued offer, accepted contract, provisioning request, invoice, payment/settlement, activation, renewal and cancellation. Pin SKU, entitlement, country pricebook version, currency, tax treatment, validity and approver. Define proration, metering, trial expiry, grace, dunning, suspension, reactivation, refund and export rules. Do not promise unlimited AI usage without an approved fair-use and cost policy.

Retain existing offer names through a catalog crosswalk: DUDOS Secure Web Rescue, AI Website, Growth & Commerce, Member/Association 360, Education 360, Business 360, Enterprise, Private, Managed Growth & Trust and White Label / Partner map into the proposed capability bundles without losing scope. Retain Basic Accounting Connect, Academy, Living Lab Enablement and Partner/Builder modules as selectable extensions. Source Starter, Professional, Enterprise, White Label, Managed Digital Operations and API/Plugin/Agent Marketplace families remain commercial grouping options. Validate exact SKU names against the retained catalog before issue.

C10 Customer service and retention

Each customer has an accountable relationship owner, delivery owner and backup. Track onboarding completion, time to first value, product adoption, support demand, reliability, invoice issues and renewal dates. Customer health must expose its inputs and missing data. Generate a proposed recovery plan when an issue persists; do not conceal service failure behind a composite score.

Support covers self-service knowledge, AI assistance, tickets, human escalation, incident communications and post-incident follow-up. Service targets use severity, business calendar and contracted coverage. Response and restoration targets are different. Provider queues, maintenance, exclusions and customer dependencies are visible in the SLA. Close a case only after evidence of resolution and the applicable acceptance rule.

C11 API event and MCP integration

Yellow v3.1 addition: C30 defines the three EADC/DAIOS/Project Brain interface gaps, source-owned Odoo bridge and the bounded four-capability DAIOS execution profile. Use versioned adapters and preserve independent outcome verification.

Publish a connector capability registry with supported versions, authentication, scopes, operations, quotas, app-review requirement, license, country eligibility, owner, last test and deprecation date. A connector's existence does not establish write or production entitlement. Treat unavailable APIs as discovery gaps with a supported manual or export/import path.

Use REST or equivalent business APIs as authoritative contracts. MCP exposes selected governed capabilities to agents through a gateway; it never bypasses tenant checks, normal API validation or approvals. Every tool has a read/write classification, resource scopes, schema, timeout, rate limit, cost budget, output redaction, owner and failure behavior. Validate token audience/resource and avoid token passthrough.

Commands carry tenant and actor context, action, object/version, correlation ID, idempotency key and authority reference. Events carry event_id, event_type, schema_version, tenant_id, entity_id, source, occurred_at, sequence/object_version, payload reference and trace context. Use transactional outbox/inbox, bounded retries, dead-letter queues, reconciliation and replay safety. Minimize personal data in event payloads.

Provider callbacks require the prescribed authenticity and server-side transaction validation, with signatures where supported, timestamp/replay controls, environment binding and durable receipt before processing. Stale credentials move the connector to degraded status with owner notification. Version upgrades run compatibility tests and customer migration checks. Report the actual business effect, not merely that a job was enqueued.

C12 AI agents and knowledge

Yellow v3.1 addition: preserve DOL A01 to A20 as mapped specializations of the retained AG roles. C27 adds action-specific policy, typed handoffs, durable receipts, source-tool schema gaps, cost/benefit definitions and provider currency review.

AI supports discovery, requirements extraction, site assessment, content generation, coding assistance, search/RAG, sales qualification, support triage, reporting, market research, anomaly diagnosis and upgrade recommendations. Use a model gateway with per-task routing and evaluation. ChatGPT/OpenAI, Gemini and other providers are candidates subject to current account capability, data terms, language quality, latency and cost.

Each agent record includes objective, source permissions, tenant scope, allowed tools, prohibited actions, task budget, memory retention, prompt/model version, evaluation set, escalation, accountable owner and kill switch. New agents start inactive. Low-risk draft generation can run under delegated policy. Publishing, production deployment, financial commitments, sensitive disclosure and high-impact personnel or academic decisions require the applicable authority check.

Treat uploaded documents, webpages, emails, retrieved snippets and tool responses as untrusted data. Their text cannot alter authority or request secret disclosure. Enforce retrieval access before search and again before output. Keep tenant documents and embeddings isolated; delete or revoke projections when source access changes. Answers provide evidence and say when the source is missing, stale or contradictory.

Measure task completion, groundedness, incorrect tool use, policy violations, latency and cost against realistic examples, including adversarial inputs. A model's own confidence does not constitute approval. Deterministic services validate finance, entitlement and workflow transitions. Logs support investigation without retaining unnecessary sensitive prompts.

Map the 25 legacy logical prompt roles to the 22 v2.1 runtime roles and D3 additions by purpose and retained ID. They are not automatically 25 deployed agents. Map EAACP A0–A5 and Alumni360 AU0–AU5 and other source autonomy labels to explicit permissions; equal numbers are not equal authority, and Alumni360 AU5 prohibits consequential autonomy.

C13 Growth analytics and opportunity discovery

Yellow v3.1 addition: C31 distinguishes competitive market intelligence from challenge competitions and maps opportunities to experiments, existing modules, owners and evidence. C33 puts CRM and revenue traceability before the first commercial pilot transaction.

Connect content and campaigns to landing visits, consented engagement, leads, qualified opportunities, orders, settled revenue, retention and expansion. After reviewing the two Google Drive areas you supplied, the ICC Bangladesh working files, your recent DUDOS and website discussions, the DAIOS/EADC/DUDOS material, the commercialisation strategy, the Digital Trust work, the Master Prompt architecture, and current public technical guidance for search, APIs, AI agents, MCP, accessibility, cybersecurity and major digital channels, my conclusion is straightforward:

You do not need another strategy document before development. You now need to freeze an executable “DUDOS Master Blueprint v1.0” and immediately build the DUDOS Control Plane + Website Transformation Factory, using ICC Bangladesh as the first complete external reference implementation.

Your existing material already defines most of the philosophy. The June DUDOS operating guidance says that Daffodil is no longer merely building websites or software; it is building an AI-powered Digital Product Factory, SaaS Engineering Organisation, Marketplace Development Hub and Global Digital Growth Engine, based on Build Once–Reuse Everywhere, Revenue Before Development, AI First, Reuse Before Build and system-generated accountability. [1] The Master Prompt Architecture independently reaches the same conclusion and explicitly recommends moving from framework design to the first foundation sprint, including reusable identity, approval, knowledge, API, billing and analytics capabilities. [2]

The EADC Founder Vision makes the intended end state even clearer: every website, SaaS product, AI solution, API, plugin, automation and integration should become AI-native, API-first, secure, reusable, commercially viable, SEO-ready, globally deployable, measurable and connected to existing Daffodil assets before new development begins. [3]

### The description I recommend freezing

DUDOS — Daffodil Unified Digital Operating System — is Daffodil’s AI-native, API-first, multi-tenant digital platform for transforming an organisation’s existing website, data, documents, digital channels and business processes into one secure, intelligent, interactive and commercially productive digital operating environment.

DUDOS can accept an organisation’s existing domain, website, database, files, Google Drive, source code, documents, images, videos, voice instructions and approved third-party systems; analyse and structure the information; reuse existing DUDOS modules where possible; generate or modernise the digital experience; connect enterprise software and authorised external APIs; and continuously operate the resulting platform through governed AI agents, automation, analytics and human accountability.

It combines website and content management, customer and member journeys, CRM, commerce, billing, payment integration, knowledge, search, AI assistants and agents, social-media orchestration, digital marketing, SEO, analytics, customer success, infrastructure, cybersecurity, backup, disaster recovery, monitoring, approvals, evidence and executive accountability.

DUDOS is not simply a website builder. The website is the public digital gateway to a reusable operating platform. Every deployment is expected to become measurable, secure, maintainable and commercially sustainable, with a path from visitor → engagement → lead → opportunity → transaction → onboarding → adoption → retention → renewal → expansion.

The same DUDOS core shall serve Daffodil Group, Daffodil Education Network, Daffodil International University and other Daffodil concerns as lighthouse customers while being packaged through DDPE for local and global customers as SaaS, managed service, white-label, private deployment, APIs, plugins, marketplace modules and industry-specific solutions.

DUDOS shall operate continuously. Governed Agentic AI shall monitor services, assist customers, detect exceptions, support marketing and sales, analyse behaviour, identify opportunities, prepare content, watch technology changes, monitor cybersecurity and infrastructure, and generate daily, weekly and monthly management intelligence. AI may automate approved low-risk work, but consequential financial, legal, security, HR, academic, regulatory or publication decisions remain subject to authorised human control.

The DUDOS measure of success is not “the site was developed”. Success is verified uptime, trusted data, customer value, qualified leads, conversion, collected revenue, adoption, retention, reusable assets, security, operational efficiency and evidence-based accountability.

That description captures the direction already present across EADC, the DUDOS team operating constitution and the commercialisation strategy. Your internal commercial strategy also recommends owning the critical control plane—identity, data, workflow, knowledge, KPI/accountability and agent orchestration—while selectively integrating or buying commodity edge services. [4]

EADC → DAIOS → DUDOS → DDPE → DECGS

## What the research and ICC Bangladesh case prove

### ICC is exactly the right reference case

The ICC Bangladesh material gives you an unusually good test of the DUDOS concept because it begins from the real-world problem DUDOS is supposed to solve: a compromised legacy website, fragmented content, third-party plugins, unclear operational ownership and an urgent need to restore a trusted public digital presence.

The ICC blueprint correctly concludes that the hacked site should not simply be restored as another plugin-heavy brochure site. It recommends a governed digital trade platform combining the public website with membership, events, finance, committees, research, knowledge, AI assistance and controlled APIs. It also explicitly states that the existing private Digital Trade Gateway is an interaction/architecture prototype rather than a completed production operating system. [5]

That distinction is extremely important for DUDOS.

Your team needs one mandatory evidence ladder for every capability:

Concept → Designed → Prototype → Integrated → Tested → Production → Commercially Packaged → Paid Customer → Revenue Proven → Scaled and Renewed

A capability shall never be described as “available in DUDOS” merely because it exists in a diagram, prompt or prototype.

For example, the ICC Update Control Manual records that the v1 prototype already has useful form and storage foundations, but says that a full enterprise CMS, member portal, billing platform and autonomous trade service are not yet complete. It also distinguishes working capabilities from illustrative ones. [6]

This evidence ladder should be added to the DUDOS Master Blueprint as a mandatory control.

### The ICC cybersecurity lesson must become a reusable DUDOS service

The ICC blueprint correctly prohibits putting a compromised WordPress/cPanel backup directly back on the internet. It calls for quarantine, forensic inspection, secret rotation, controlled migration and off-site immutable backup rather than blind restoration. [5]

That should become a commercial product:

DUDOS Secure Web Rescue

Its standard workflow should be:

Compromised Site → Isolate / Quarantine → Preserve Evidence → Inventory Domain, DNS, Email, Hosting and Credentials → Rotate Credentials and Keys → Scan and Analyse Legacy Files → Extract Approved Business Content → Map URLs and SEO Equity → Rebuild from Trusted Components → Migrate Approved Data Only → Security Test → Redirect Old URLs → Launch Behind WAF/CDN → Monitor → Maintain Clean Recovery Copies

This is commercially stronger than advertising “website development”. It solves a high-value business risk.

### The modern website market supports your platform model

Current mainstream platforms increasingly separate front-end experience from structured business services. Webflow exposes CMS, page, component, asset, form, ecommerce and webhook capabilities through APIs; Wix Headless allows multiple custom front ends to share Wix business capabilities; Shopify operates through a versioned API ecosystem; and HubSpot exposes CRM, CMS, marketing, automation and webhook APIs. [7]

The implication is not that DUDOS should rebuild every feature these companies have.

The correct positioning is:

DUDOS owns the governance, identity, data contracts, customer model, orchestration, AI, knowledge, reusable business modules, revenue control and accountability. Commodity functions may be built, integrated, bought, white-labelled or consumed by API according to speed, quality, ownership, risk and commercial return.

That is already consistent with your internal Build–Buy–White Label–Open Source–SaaS logic. [1]

### AI, API and MCP need one architectural rule

API and MCP should not be treated as interchangeable.

A normal business API remains the governed system contract for operations such as customers, membership, payment, content, CRM, HR, products or transactions.

MCP should sit above or beside that API layer as an AI tool-access protocol. OpenAI’s current MCP documentation describes it as a standard way for applications to expose tools and context to models and explicitly advises trusted servers, least-privilege credentials, tool filtering and approval for sensitive actions. [8]

Therefore:

Business System → Governed API / Event → DUDOS API Gateway → Authorization / Tenant / Audit / Rate Policy → MCP Tool Adapter (where AI needs it) → Registered AI Agent → Human Approval when required

Never allow MCP to become a back door around identity, API governance, tenant isolation, audit or approval.

Modern agent frameworks also provide mechanisms for guardrails, hand-offs, tracing and human approval of sensitive tool calls. [9] That fits the AI Agent Registry and human-accountability model you have already defined.

Your current Module Registry, Prompt Registry and Agent Registry are strong foundations. I would add three operational registries—not as another strategic layer, but as executable DUDOS data tables.

This is how DUDOS knows that a forgotten site, certificate, account or channel has become a risk.

#### Connector Capability and Version Registry

For every platform connector, maintain:

Platform → API family → Current supported version → Owner → Authentication method → Scopes → Read capabilities → Write capabilities → Publishing capability → Analytics capability → Webhook capability → Rate/quota limits → App-review requirement → Human-consent requirement → Current status → Deprecation date → Last tested → Replacement path

This is vital because platforms change. LinkedIn, for example, uses versioned marketing APIs and has explicit sunset dates for old versions. [10] YouTube applies OAuth, quotas and application compliance controls to publishing operations. [11]

DUDOS should therefore never hard-code an assumption that a connector “will always work”.

#### Technology and Platform Change Registry

A Technology Watch Agent should continuously monitor only legitimate public information such as:

vendor release notes;

official developer changelogs;

API deprecations;

security advisories;

supported model updates;

search-engine documentation;

social-platform policy changes;

CMS/plugin versions;

cloud/platform changes;

public competitor features and pricing;

standards updates.

Every detected change becomes:

CHANGE-ID → → Source → → Date → → Confidence → → Affected DUDOS layer → → Affected module/agent/product → → Severity → → Recommended action → → Owner → → Deadline → → Test evidence → → Release decision

This is the correct interpretation of your requirement that DUDOS “understand algorithm changes”.

DUDOS cannot legitimately claim access to Meta, Google, YouTube, LinkedIn or TikTok’s private recommendation algorithms. Instead, it should monitor official APIs, published policies, changelogs and the customer’s own performance signals, detect anomalies, run controlled experiments and recommend adjustments. Your Digital Trust work already warns that there is no universal cross-platform private-data control API and recommends official platform integrations first, with manual/evidence routes retained. [12]

That distinction will protect DUDOS credibility.

## V2-C. Physical system, ownership and integration specification

### C1. Deployable architecture and reuse decision

Start with the smallest supported system that can prove a complete customer lifecycle. Retain the verified Odoo/Daffodil governance and business assets where suitable, expose controlled APIs, and keep AI inference, large-file processing and search in bounded services. Reuse the installed Java, Python or other production stack when evidence supports it. If a new web experience is needed, Next.js/React with TypeScript is a candidate, not a mandate to rewrite working systems.

The initial deployment comprises an authenticated portal/API, the selected transactional authority systems, durable workers, PostgreSQL, object storage, a search projection, an AI gateway and observability. Use managed database/backups where the operating cost and data-location requirements justify them. Separate development, test, staging, production and clean-room recovery accounts/configurations. Do not share live credentials or unrestricted production data with teaching or coding environments.

Introduce dedicated microservices, Kubernetes, a separate search cluster or a large event platform only when measured throughput, isolation, availability or team ownership requires them. Each addition needs an owner, support horizon, recovery plan, licence, infrastructure cost and exit strategy. A catalogue of tools is not an architecture.

### C2. Tenant and login layers

The platform supports public visitors, customer users, customer administrators, merchant operators, partners/resellers/builders, students, instructors/supervisors, provider support, developers, finance, auditors, security operators, tenant administrators and tightly controlled platform administrators. Machine identities have separate scoped delegations; they do not inherit a human administrator's entire account.

Use SSO/OIDC where available, MFA/passkeys for privileged and financial roles, short-lived sessions, device/session revocation and periodic access recertification. Support impersonation requires a recorded support purpose, time limit, visible banner and audit; hide secrets and prevent sensitive actions unless separately authorised. Break-glass access is independent, monitored, time-limited and reviewed after use.

Role grants alone are insufficient. Evaluate tenant, legal entity, branch, record ownership, data sensitivity, consent/purpose, action and workflow state server-side. Apply the same rule to APIs, media URLs, caches, exports, logs, search snippets, vector retrieval, reporting and background jobs. Platform administrators should not routinely read all tenant business data. Provider support must work through scoped access and escalation.

These DUDOS routes are proposed contracts, not live endpoints. Each request validates server-derived tenant/actor context, schema, purpose, scope, object version and rate policy. Use OAuth/OIDC or appropriate service credentials held in a vault; use PKCE where applicable for interactive OAuth. Never accept a tenant ID in a body as authority. Return consistent error codes, field errors, correlation ID and retry guidance without leaking secrets or tenant existence.

Every command with an external effect uses a durable business idempotency key. Each event includes event_id, type, schema_version, occurred_at UTC, tenant_id, object_id, object_version, actor/delegation, correlation_id and evidence reference. Persist state and outbox atomically; consumers maintain an inbox and unique business-effect key. Handle concurrency with row/version checks, provider limits with bounded backoff, and poison jobs with owned dead letters.

Test the failure between provider success and local acknowledgement. Replaying the job must reconcile the original payment/message/payout rather than repeat it. Never use a single delivery attempt or event timestamp as financial truth. Confirm stale/out-of-order events against the provider's current object. API contracts include pagination, batch limits, timeout, schema compatibility, deprecation, reconciliation cadence and exit export.

### C5. MCP and plugin gateway

MCP exposes selected tools over governed business APIs; it is not a replacement for those APIs or an escape from their permissions. Register server provenance, transport, OAuth/resource audience, supported protocol version, tool-schema hash, scopes, risk, timeout, data destination and revocation. Allowlist tools per agent/task. Treat retrieved documents, tool descriptions and customer uploads as untrusted input that cannot rewrite system policy.

Use sandboxed execution, approved egress destinations, secure temporary files, output validation and log redaction. Prohibit unrestricted shell/network/database tools for customer agents. Sensitive actions use an approval token bound to the exact object/action/version/limits. Do not pass bearer tokens through a third-party MCP server as a shortcut. Connector changes trigger revalidation, not automatic trust. [W13]

### C6. Search and customer intelligence

Start with indexed exact IDs, names, contact identifiers, organisations, products, SKUs, quote/contract numbers, domains, tickets and document titles. Add lexical full-text search and semantic retrieval for natural-language questions. Filters include authorised tenant, legal entity, people/role, sector, country, relationship stage, date, owner, source, status, language and access classification. Deduplicate carefully and support controlled merge/split with an audit trail.

Perform access filtering before ranking, snippets, counts, suggestions or model context. Store source/version/hash, ACL version, effective/expiry dates, locale, owner and retention. Remove or quarantine revoked/deleted/superseded content across indexes, caches, vectors and answer history according to policy. A public profile projection contains only approved fields. Cross-customer sales analysis requires an expressly authorised aggregate scope and appropriate de-identification.

The answer view cites accessible sources, separates fact from recommendation, shows material uncertainty and provides the next permitted action. It abstains when evidence is missing. Evaluate known customer-search questions, typo/locale handling, identifier precision, stale data, no-result usefulness, permission leakage and latency. Search logs themselves are access-controlled and minimised; do not turn queries into an unrestricted staff/customer surveillance record.

Google Drive can also be connected through user-authorised scopes; a least-privilege design should request only the files/folders necessary rather than broad access. [14]

### The intake wizard should ask business questions, not only technical questions

The minimum questionnaire should cover:

Organisation and authority: legal/brand name, authorised owner, approving authority, target countries, languages, domain ownership and responsible contacts.

Business: objectives, customers/members, offerings, products, services, prices, key journeys, current problems, desired outcomes, revenue targets and success KPIs.

Existing digital estate: domain, hosting, website/CMS, source code, database, analytics, Search Console, integrations, email, forms, social profiles, ad accounts, applications and current vendors.

Content: pages, documents, leadership, services, products, events, publications, photos, videos, FAQs, policies and languages.

Business systems: CRM, ERP, HR, LMS, finance, membership, ticketing, inventory, payment and any internal database.

Growth: audiences, search markets, keywords already known, social channels, campaign history, current lead sources and conversion points.

Risk and compliance: personal/sensitive data, payment, regulated activity, retention, legal requirements, accessibility and countries served.

Operations: expected uptime, support hours, SLA, escalation contacts, desired backup destinations, RPO/RTO and managed-service requirements.

Commercial package: DUDOS edition, optional modules, AI usage, number of administrators/users, hosting model, implementation tier and white-label requirement.

### DUDOS then classifies the transformation

There should be three delivery paths.

#### Enhance in place

Use when an existing website is healthy and commercially sensible to retain.

DUDOS connects through APIs and adds:

AI assistants;

CRM;

analytics;

SEO governance;

social orchestration;

forms/workflow;

customer success;

monitoring;

DECGS;

external business-system integration.

#### Headless or hybrid transformation

Use when the existing backend still has business value but the public experience is outdated.

DUDOS creates a modern frontend and accesses structured business functionality via APIs.

This is increasingly practical because modern website and commerce platforms expose headless/API capabilities. [15]

#### Clean rebuild and migration

Use when the existing system is:

compromised;

unsupported;

highly plugin-dependent;

unmaintainable;

inaccessible;

structurally poor;

commercially unsuitable.

### Your “15–30 minute website” ambition should be defined correctly

DUDOS should aim to produce a first structured visual preview very quickly once valid information is supplied.

## Infrastructure, cybersecurity, resilience and compliance

For DUDOS to become a trusted global platform, this is non-negotiable.

### Reference runtime architecture

I recommend the following vendor-neutral architecture:

INTERNET → CDN / DNS / WAF / DDoS → Experience Gateway → Website/PWA             Mobile                Chat/Voice → API Gateway → Identity/Tenant      Business Services       AI Gateway → Workflow/Event Bus       Agent Runtime → Model Router/RAG → Transaction DB       Knowledge/Search → Object Storage       Vector/Graph Layer → Analytics / BI → DECGS

Alongside it:

Secrets Management → CI/CD → Observability → Security Telemetry → Audit → Backups → Disaster Recovery → Cost/FinOps → Asset Registry

The current Daffodil commercialisation work already recommends a multi-tenant SaaS architecture with tenant-aware identity, explicit APIs, event-driven integrations, audit-first design, model routing, object storage and observability. [4]

### Security baseline

DUDOS should adopt a contractual security baseline rather than the vague phrase “highly secure”.

Minimum controls should include:

MFA and least privilege;

server-side RBAC/ABAC;

tenant isolation;

encrypted transport/storage;

secrets vault;

protected admin interfaces;

API rate and abuse controls;

secure OAuth;

dependency and supply-chain scanning;

code scanning;

SAST/DAST where appropriate;

Web Application Firewall;

secure headers;

logging and immutable audit;

vulnerability management;

security incident workflow;

phishing and malicious-URL protection;

secure software-development lifecycle;

penetration testing before major production releases;

customer-specific data retention and deletion;

independent restore tests.

The current NIST Cybersecurity Framework treats cybersecurity as a continuous Govern–Identify–Protect–Detect–Respond–Recover discipline rather than only perimeter protection, while zero-trust guidance removes implicit trust based simply on network location. [21]

For application verification, OWASP ASVS provides testable application security requirements; AI-specific systems should also be assessed against current AI-security controls rather than assuming conventional web security is sufficient. [22]

The ICC controls already embody several of these principles: server-side authorisation, tenant scoping, four-eye controls, protected documents, reversible releases and retained evidence. [6]

### Bangladesh compliance is now a real design consideration

As of September 2026, Bangladesh has enacted updated data and cyber legislation, including the Personal Data Protection Act 2026 and cyber/data-governance legislation published through the official Government Press. [23]

Accordingly, DUDOS needs a jurisdiction and compliance profile per tenant.

Do not advertise “100% compliant everywhere”.

Instead:

Country → Applicable Data Requirements → Sector Requirements → Consent Model → Data Location → Retention → Cross-Border Rules → Payment Rules → Terms / Privacy → Required Human/Legal Validation → Evidence

For payments, DUDOS should preferably integrate licensed/acquiring/payment providers rather than attempting to become the payment operator itself. Payment architecture should use provider-hosted/tokenised checkout, verified webhooks, reconciliation and controlled receipts, matching the ICC blueprint’s design. [5]

### Accessibility is part of trust and marketability

DUDOS should make WCAG 2.2 AA the default accessibility target for web products, with automatic and manual accessibility testing built into release gates. The ICC documents already use this direction, and WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C accessibility recommendation. [6] [24]

### Four-layer backup must be frozen

Your backup requirement should become:

Layer A — Production Backup → Frequent operational backup → Layer B — Independent Account/Provider Backup → Different security boundary → Layer C — Geographic/Region Recovery Copy → Separate location → Layer D — Immutable Critical Archive → Protected against alteration/ransomware

Then add the customer option you specifically requested:

Layer E — Customer-Controlled Recovery Export → Encrypted scheduled copy to a customer-controlled → Google Drive / approved object store / enterprise repository

The customer copy should contain:

backup manifest;

timestamp;

version;

database export or restorable snapshot;

content/media;

configuration export;

integrity checksum;

encryption metadata;

application release identifier;

restoration instructions.

However, the customer’s Google Drive copy must not replace the primary disaster-recovery system. It is an additional portability/ownership copy.

That is an important competitive differentiator:

“Your data and recovery package remain portable and independently retrievable.”

The ICC blueprint’s “exit-ready” principle likewise requires the customer to retain ownership/control over data, domains, source, configuration, documentation and credentials. [5]

### Build a public DUDOS Trust Centre

To earn trust rather than merely claim it, the DUDOS public site should expose a controlled Trust Centre containing:

service-status page;

privacy statement;

security overview;

data-processing model;

accessibility statement;

backup/recovery approach;

responsible security-reporting route;

official domains/channels;

API status;

incident communication policy;

AI-use principles;

data ownership/export principles;

subprocessor/provider information where required;

service/version release notes;

verified compliance reports/certificates when actually obtained.

The operative word is verified. Do not display certifications that have not been achieved.

Do not rely on an obsolete ordinance, draft regulation or legacy document simply because a familiar title appears. [W22, W23]

For each additional country, verify local company/trade permissions, privacy/data transfer, electronic signatures, consumer protection, tax/VAT/GST/e-invoicing, payment/banking, employment/student work, education rules and regulated-sector activity. Consider GDPR/European AI obligations only when their territorial/material scope applies; similarly evaluate U.S., UK, Indian and other rules against actual facts. This blueprint supplies the workflow and fields, not a pre-certified legal outcome in every market.

### F2. Agreement and NDA assembly

The contract engine assembles counsel-approved clauses into a master service agreement, SOW/order form, SLA, DPA/security schedule, NDA, staff/contractor agreement, partner/reseller/affiliate terms, merchant integration terms, student/Living Lab participation agreement, academic delivery agreement and exit schedule. Choose the jurisdiction, legal parties and signer authority before issue. Do not use a generic NDA as a substitute for data-processing, IP or employment terms.

| Document | Minimum decisions and clause fields | Execution control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MSA + SOW | Parties, scope, milestones, acceptance, exclusions, fees/tax, change, warranty, limits/liability, dispute and notices | Exact offer/scope versions; authorised signatures and effective date |
| SLA + security/DPA | Coverage/clocks, severity, remedies, data roles, purposes, processors, location, retention, incidents and audit | Funded service capability; local legal review and approved obligations |
| Mutual or one-way NDA | Discloser/recipient, purpose, definition, exclusions, permitted recipients, care, compelled disclosure, term, return/destruction and survival | Role-appropriate access; confidentiality training and lawful retention carve-outs |
| Staff / contractor | Role, deliverables, estimate/reporting, confidentiality, security, IP/licence, subcontracting, conflicts, payment and offboarding | Appropriate work status, competence and access approval; no automatic HR determination |
| Partner / merchant | Seller/platform role, claims, customer ownership, commissions, refunds, disputes, support, prohibited conduct and exit | Identity/payment/tax eligibility; versioned commission schedule |
| Academy / Living Lab | Academic responsibility, work status/hours, supervision, consent, safeguarding, IP, disclosures, earnings and complaints | Institution/local approval; no compulsory live sales for grades |

Store template version, negotiated deviations, document hash, signature identity/authority, timestamps, effective/expiry dates and obligation IDs. Changes generate a successor, never alter the signed file. The system reminds owners of notice periods, deliverables, renewals and expiring NDAs/access. Preserve executed documents under retention/legal-hold rules; a generic deletion request must not erase records that must lawfully be retained.

### F3. Security baseline and operating safeguards

Threat-model each deployment, including account takeover, phishing, malicious uploads, cross-tenant exposure, injection, supply-chain compromise, insecure plugins, API abuse, credential theft, fraudulent bank-detail change, ransomware and staff departure. Use least privilege/MFA, vault-managed keys, encryption, private storage, protected admin, WAF/rate controls, safe upload quarantine, dependency/code/container scans, SBOM, signed releases and vulnerability remediation. Pin the applicable OWASP ASVS version and security test scope. [W25]

Use two-person verification for payment-beneficiary changes, domain transfer and critical recovery-key actions. Authenticate email domains and train staff on phishing/reporting; do not rely only on filtering. Build account recovery without dependence on a single person's phone or mailbox. Keep an external incident contact/status route and an inventory of registrar, DNS, cloud, billing, email and encryption recovery dependencies.

Hosted/tokenized checkout reduces card-data handling but does not make DUDOS or a merchant automatically PCI compliant. Determine the integration-specific validation scope with the acquirer/provider or qualified assessor, including applicable ecommerce script/website requirements. Avoid raw card data in logs, templates, support tickets or AI. [W21]

### F4. Backup layers and portability contract

| Layer | Purpose and proposed implementation | Proof required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — operational | Automated database PITR/snapshots and application/media backup | Freshness, complete base/WAL chain and scheduled restore evidence |
| B — independent security boundary | Copy to a separate account; use an independent provider for a whole-provider threat | Separate privileged identity/billing/recovery; tested read access during primary lockout |
| C — geographic recovery | Approved second region/location under residency/transfer rules | Recover application dependencies and data when the primary region fails |
| D — immutable archive | Retention-locked/WORM critical snapshots and audit artifacts | Retention/deletion controls, protected keys and a successful recovery drill |
| E — customer-controlled export | Optional hourly/daily/on-demand encrypted package to approved customer storage | Manifest, delivery receipt, checksum, decrypt/re-import proof and failure alert |

Layers describe failure boundaries and controls, not a requirement to purchase five unrelated storage products. Record when a copy satisfies multiple properties and what correlated failure remains. Four folders in one account do not supply independent protection. Replication alone can copy corruption; a backup alone cannot provide instant failover. Object Lock protects retained versions, but key loss, bad source data and missing dependencies can still prevent recovery. [W11, W12]

The recovery manifest covers database/schema and transaction position, media/documents, source/release artifacts, infrastructure as code, configuration, dependency locks, DNS/zone export, event/job ledger, audit/evidence, identity configuration, key references, integrity hashes and restoration instructions. Protect secrets and private keys in a recoverable vault path; do not bundle plaintext secrets in customer downloads. A database file without compatible application/configuration is not an exit-ready system.

Allow customer destinations such as an approved object store, enterprise repository, SFTP endpoint or appropriately authorised Drive folder. Validate ownership, destination security, residency, capacity, retention, key custody and permitted transfer before enabling. Show last successful export, due next, size, hash, receipt and last restore test. Capture hourly/daily cadence, timezone, full/incremental strategy and expected recovery granularity; avoid claiming hourly RPO from a daily full export.

### F5. Service tiers and disaster recovery

| Proposed tier | Workload/design | Proposed recovery objective, subject to testing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | Noncritical public content; automated backups and restore runbook | RPO up to 24 hours; RTO up to 8 hours |
| Business | Customer workflows and commerce integration; PITR, redundant application, independent copies | RPO up to 15 minutes; RTO up to 2 hours |
| Critical | Explicitly justified transactions; tested HA, warm standby and independent recovery | RPO target up to 5 minutes; RTO target up to 60 minutes |

These are planning options, not signed SLAs or measured claims. Set workload-specific targets, retention, maintenance window, availability SLO and funding in the customer policy. Async replication can lose recent writes; synchronous designs impose latency/availability trade-offs and may still face correlated failures. State the maximum accepted data-loss exposure and outage scenario explicitly. Record measured results from drills before selling the target.

Automatic failover is permitted only for a pre-approved infrastructure failure pattern with healthy replication, available keys, compatible release, capacity and a fenced single writer. Use quorum/lease/fencing to prevent two primaries. After promotion, re-establish jobs/outbox processing, reconcile provider effects, route traffic and run synthetic checks. DNS TTL and caching, external providers and session continuity affect recovery time. Failback is a planned reconciliation/change operation, not an uncontrolled oscillation.

A suspected cyber compromise uses containment, evidence preservation and clean-room restoration; automatic promotion of potentially compromised state is blocked. Recover in dependency order: emergency identity/keys and network → infrastructure/artifacts → authoritative databases → objects/configuration → workers/integrations → read models/search → user journeys → reconciliation and controlled traffic. Test regional outage, lost cloud account, ransomware/corruption, key recovery, registrar access and customer export. Proposed cadence: daily automated integrity/freshness checks, monthly sampled restore and quarterly cross-boundary disaster exercise; confirm risk-based cadence and funding.

### F6. Daily diagnosis to verified action

The daily report covers availability/latency/errors, saturation and cost, backup freshness and replication lag, restore-test age, export receipts, domain/TLS/renewal risks, vulnerability/identity anomalies, queue age/dead letters, webhook/reconciliation gaps, AI failures/cost/quality, consent/message delivery, overdue work, customer complaints and health, merchant exceptions, commissions/payouts, learning/lab controls and upcoming vendor/policy changes.

Every observation includes source/time window, confidence, impact, severity, affected tenant/object/version, primary/backup owner, due date, recommended action, allowed automatic remedy, evidence and closure test. A deterministic rule establishes measurable exceptions; AI explains and groups them. Known-noise suppression has an owner, reason and expiry. A ticket closes only when the original signal and acceptance check are verified.

An independent heartbeat detects missed reports, failed schedulers, inaccessible telemetry and broken notifications. Route urgent cases immediately; do not wait for the daily summary. DECGS receives authorised evidence projections and management decisions. Daily reports are generated for the appropriate audience, with sensitive data redacted and customer/provider views separated. [W33]
