## V2-G. Commerce, accounting, ecosystem and Academy

### G1. Instant commerce integration with clear responsibility

Offer three paths: add a hosted store/link or approved commerce block to an existing site; install a reviewed plugin on a healthy supported CMS; or connect a headless store through a versioned API. Shopify and WooCommerce are candidate adapters, selected against merchant country, ownership, cost, maintenance, product model and required plugins. Existing merchant systems may remain authoritative. A compromised CMS follows the rescue route first. [W16–W18]

Onboarding records legal seller, store owner, country, business/tax eligibility, catalog, product restrictions, currency, prices/tax, inventory source, shipping zones/rates, fulfilment, returns/refunds, customer service, payment merchant and privacy/marketing choices. DUDOS provides configuration, templates and workflows. The merchant owns product legality, stock, pricing, delivery, warranties and customer remedies unless a specific agreement lawfully allocates another role. DUDOS must not become seller of record or a money custodian by default.

Core journeys cover product/variant/search, cart, availability/reservation, checkout, invoice/receipt, payment verification, fulfilment, tracking, cancellation, return, partial/full refund, dispute and support. Optional capabilities include booking, digital downloads, subscriptions, B2B quotes, POS, cash on delivery, local delivery and marketplace integrations. Activate each only when the provider and country support it. Do not promise every plugin works with every site.

Payments use server-created checkout sessions and provider-confirmed state. For SSLCOMMERZ, implement IPN plus the Order Validation API and compare expected merchant/transaction/amount/currency; a browser return is not sufficient. For other gateways, use the documented validation/signature and reconciliation flow. Handle fees, settlement delay, risk holds and refunds separately. Reconcile merchant gross sales, collected cash, invoices, stock and commissions. [W15, W30]

### G2. Basic accounting with a controlled chart of accounts

The basic accounting product supports a legal-entity-specific chart of accounts, customers/suppliers, sales/purchase invoices, receipts/payments, expenses, tax configuration, journals, reconciliation, period close, trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, cash/bank reporting and aging. Start with a verified accounting engine and localised configuration; build a new ledger only if the reuse and statutory-fit assessment shows a genuine gap.

Allow users to customise account codes/names/hierarchy, cost centres and reporting labels while controlling account types, posting rules, control accounts and historical mappings. Typical groups are assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses; example accounts in the workbook are starter configuration, not mandatory tax advice. Opening balances require balanced supporting evidence. Retire or remap an account prospectively; do not rewrite historical journals to fit a new label.

Every posted journal belongs to one legal entity, period and currency context, has balanced debit/credit lines, source document, actor and approval, and is immutable. Corrections use linked reversals/adjustments. Restrict backdating and posting to closed periods; reopening needs authority and an audit. Use decimal/minor-unit arithmetic, the currency's actual precision and finance-approved FX/tax rules. Mixed currencies cannot be added without an explicit conversion model.

Payment gateway settlement is reconciled as gross receipts less provider fees/refunds/withholdings, not simply booked as revenue. Subscription cash may create deferred revenue depending on the approved accounting policy. Third-party merchant gross merchandise value is not DUDOS revenue. Student/partner commission obligations belong to the liable contracting entity and are separate from DUDOS subscription income. AI may suggest categorisation; it must not invent journal evidence or autonomously file statutory returns.

The workbook includes a journal review aid and commission calculator with blank real-data inputs. They are review templates, not a full accounting system. Production needs transaction isolation, unique source keys, period controls, reconciliation, immutable audit and finance-reviewed statements. Use an established country-compliant accounting/tax connector for needs beyond the basic scope, including payroll, consolidation, complex inventory valuation or statutory filing.

### G3. Expert, reseller, builder and affiliate ecosystem

Partner onboarding captures verified identity/legal entity, role, operating country, skills/certification evidence, conflicts, eligibility, NDA/IP/security terms, support obligations, tax and payout details, permitted customers/modules and review expiry. Separate reseller selling rights, affiliate referral rights, builder implementation rights, merchant product responsibilities and expert advisory scope. Partners see their contracts, assignments, customers within delegation, performance evidence and earnings; they cannot browse all tenants.

An opportunity has source, consent, attribution owner, qualification, duplicate/ownership resolution, acceptance and next action. A commission rule states version, applicable programme, attribution method/window, eligible revenue basis, rate/tier/cap, tax/fee exclusions, settlement requirement, refund/chargeback hold, currency/FX, threshold, payout timing, clawback and dispute/appeal. Show estimated, pending, earned, payable, paid, reversed and disputed separately. Referral registration alone creates no earnings.

Pay only verified payable obligations through a country-eligible bank or licensed provider under the agreed contract. Check beneficiary changes independently, reconcile provider receipts, prevent duplicate payout IDs and retain tax/withholding evidence. If automatic split payment/payout is unavailable, use an approved finance review/bank batch with reconciliation; do not invent a universal banking API or retain client money in an unlicensed wallet. No recruitment-driven or multi-level commission model is implied.

Monitor misleading claims, self-referrals, duplicate leads, consent violations and quality failures through evidence-based review. Provide appeal, correction and accountable suspension; avoid AI-only accusations or opaque penalties. Partnership/manual records, renewal, access recertification and exit remain in the system, so continuation does not depend on one employee.

Serious unresolved authority, data or financial-integrity failures require remediation regardless of aggregate marks. Provide equivalent simulations for students who cannot or should not do live sales. Sales volume, income and customer spending must not determine academic grades.

Follow-up records include enrolment/consent, attendance, prerequisite gaps, weekly competency evidence, feedback, resubmission, mentoring, accessibility accommodations, academic integrity/AI disclosure, moderation, appeal and course-version mapping. Instructors verify assessed evidence and approve grades. Retain only necessary learning data under institution policy; do not mix staff-performance files, customer private data and student portfolios.

### G5. Lecture, documentary and class production system

Every weekly lesson is generated from the approved course version and current DUDOS release. Its template includes learning outcomes, prerequisites, reading/source versions, a 120-minute seminar plan, worked demonstration, hands-on lab, field/simulation task, quiz with answer rationale, assessment rubric, common errors, accessibility adaptations and follow-up. A suggested seminar structure is 15 minutes case review, 35 concepts, 35 demonstration, 25 guided exercise and 10 reflection. Validate the actual software steps before teaching.

For each lesson, produce slides/notes, instructor script, student worksheet, dataset or sandbox snapshot, demo repository/configuration, captioned recording/transcript and an evidence checklist. The documentary template captures learner/merchant consent, story purpose, baseline, scenes, interview questions, factual/earnings claims, rights, captions, credits, reviewers and publication permission. Private customer information must be redacted; no scripted testimonial may be presented as an authentic quotation.

Example lecture, Week 12: demonstrate a sandbox sale of 100 units of currency with a 10-unit refund; reconcile the 90 eligible units to the agreed commission basis. If the signed exercise rule explicitly allows a 10% commission on that basis, estimated commission is 9 units before any separate tax/withholding policy. Then show why an unsettled payment, unresolved return, missing beneficiary or unapproved rule cannot become payable. Compare invoice revenue, cash, gateway fees and commission liability; require a balanced journal and explain that the example numbers are teaching data, not DUDOS prices or a recommended commercial rate.

Use LMS external services or approved LTI integration for enrolment, learning access and evidence exchange. Keep grades/credentials authoritative in the institution's LMS/SIS. Match API permissions and versions; never assume every LMS supports identical LTI or grading methods. Course and software releases have separate versions, compatibility notes and migration/retirement plans. [W19]

### G6. Living Lab operating charter

Each Lab binds one institution/supervisor, participating eligible merchants, students, approved products/services, locations, channels, dates and budget. DUDOS powers the website/tools, CRM, content studio, evidence, commerce adapters, support and learning records. Third-party merchants sell and fulfil products. Students may conduct authorised acquisition, marketing, service and closing activities within local work and programme rules; they do not use a DUDOS account to impersonate the merchant or spend without limits.

Onboarding checks age/work eligibility, safeguarding where relevant, supervision, participation/recording consent, work status/hours, confidentiality, IP, payment/tax eligibility, complaint/appeal routes and clear commission terms. Do not charge recruitment fees or require students to buy stock. Do not promise earnings or pressure friends/family into purchases. Affiliate disclosures, truthful offers, data minimisation and respectful opt-out are practical assessed skills.

The lab moves through sandbox training, competence check, merchant/institution approval, restricted live access, supervised operation, reconciliation and review. Role boundaries prevent students from seeing full customer datasets, changing gateway/bank details, issuing refunds, posting accounting entries or granting production access. A supervisor reviews campaigns and high-risk communications; the system enforces approved spend and frequency limits. If live eligibility is unavailable, use the equivalent simulation without academic disadvantage.

Track customer acquisition source, contact permission, activity, offer, order, settlement, returns, commission state, payout receipt, hours and learning evidence. Separate educational evidence from legally required commercial records. Report conversion and service outcomes alongside complaints, refund rates, policy violations and learning progress. Remove access promptly when the placement ends while retaining lawful evidence and resolving outstanding commissions.

## V2-H. Commercial model, implementation programme and completion

### H1. Sustainable packaging and purchasing

Retain the ten v1.0 package families. Add optional Commerce Connect, Basic Accounting Connect, DUDOS Academy, Living Lab Enablement and Partner/Builder Programme as catalogue modules rather than forcing every customer to buy them. Each SKU defines outcome, eligibility, included volumes, limits, dependencies, activation cost, recurring/usage basis, service level, exclusions, third-party charges, owner and exit support.

Price from cost and customer value, using approved country/currency pricebooks. Separate implementation, monthly/annual subscription, metered AI/messages/storage, hosting/recovery, managed content/growth, integration maintenance, education delivery and third-party pass-through. Ad spend and merchant gross sales are not DUDOS subscription revenue. No arbitrary public prices are invented in this blueprint.

Use the workbook's unit-economics model to calculate contribution from recurring revenue less direct infrastructure, AI/tools, messaging, support labour, partner commissions and payment fees. Include onboarding/migration effort, backup/restore drills, security, compliance, training, vendor support and exit costs in pricing decisions. Allocate shared costs by a disclosed driver; keep setup/one-off and recurring profitability separate. Set minimum margin and cash runway requirements through finance approval, not AI optimism.

Budget is a parameterised function of tenants, users, transactions, media/storage, retention copies, tokens/tool calls, messages, API workload, support hours, resilience tier and country obligations. Confirm exact vendor rates and contracts before signing a customer offer. Stress test lower adoption, higher support demand, provider price increase, currency movement, refunds and outage cost. A product can be technically available and commercially unsuitable; the system must show both.

### H2. Phased execution with evidence, not an unqualified date promise

| Phase | Deliverable and exit evidence | Proposed sequencing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 — baseline and current state | Source/authority decisions, Odoo/current-system proof, owners, budget, country pilot and approved scope | First 1–2 weeks after mobilisation; validate capacity |
| 1 — lifecycle foundation | Tenant/roles, profile/importer, templates, permissions, assets, audit, durable jobs and draft proposal | Next 2–4 weeks; demonstrate one complete draft customer |
| 2 — delivery and operation | Staging factory, content/search, integrations, support, backups/restore and release evidence | Next 3–6 weeks; launch one approved low-risk pilot |
| 3 — commercial proof | Pricebook, ledger/gateway reconciliation, renewal, diagnostics and measured service outcomes | In parallel where dependencies are ready; prove real reconciliation |
| 4 — commerce and partners | Merchant adapter, accounting bridge, commission/payout controls and partner portal | After payment/legal/ledger dependencies; supervised pilot |
| 5 — Academy and Living Lab | Approved curriculum, sandbox, instructor preparation, assessments and restricted lab | Course readiness before any live student selling |
| 6 — scale and resilience | More country packs, higher recovery tier, verified connectors, cost/performance evidence | Release by demand and proof, not all-at-once expansion |

These are planning ranges, not delivery commitments. The delivery lead converts them to estimated work packets, dependency graph, skill/capacity plan, acceptance criteria and customer-approved dates. Maintain the original Day-90 ambition as a pilot objective subject to verified starting assets, team capacity and scope; do not promise all global sectors and integrations within 90 days.

### H3. Acceptance scenarios added to the original 40

The expanded acceptance register covers: all 41 sheets importing without lost IDs; wrong-customer token detection; missing source body; candidate/frozen authority conflict; cross-tenant search/export; expired signing authority; changed quote/version; duplicate webhook after crash; unsupported country/gateway; commission refund/chargeback; beneficiary fraud; unbalanced journal/closed period; inventory oversell; inaccessible checkout; suppressed messaging; withdrawn content/rights; agent injection and provider fallback; lost cloud account; corrupt/ransomware restore; single-writer failover and controlled failback; missed diagnostic heartbeat; staff handover; learner access isolation; unapproved student spend; course/evidence version mismatch; customer exit/re-import; and vendor licence/API retirement.

Each selected requirement maps to design, work item, test, result, evidence and exact release. Keep the original 16 DUDOS gates, plus the applicable constitutional and specialist requirements through the crosswalk. Zero unresolved critical blockers is required where policy specifies a hard gate; do not average away a failure. The final GO records the release hash, environment/domain, approvers, rollback, service readiness and post-launch verification.

### H4. Limitations and matching routes

| Limitation | Required solution or fallback |
| --- | --- |
| A form or prompt cannot prove production readiness | Build in staging; independent tests, recovery evidence and exact-version release approval |
| A consumer AI subscription does not operate the production platform | Separate API account/gateway, budget, infrastructure and duty coverage |
| No provider exposes every social action or private algorithm | Official capability registry; approved third-party adapter or manual publishing route |
| Payment, tax and payout availability differ by country | Eligible licensed gateway/bank, local accounting/tax connector and country launch review |
| Basic accounting cannot cover every statutory/industry requirement | Integrate a verified local accounting system and specialist review |
| Replication/immutable storage cannot guarantee zero loss | Workload-specific RPO/RTO, independent keys/copies, tested clean-room recovery and honest contracts |
| AI can hallucinate or misuse tools | Cited authorised knowledge, deterministic controls, evaluations, budgets and accountable escalation |
| No universal legal/compliance certification | Official-source applicability register and qualified local review |
| Missing current template bodies/approvals | Preserve known IDs and gaps; obtain/approve the canonical source before formal adoption |
| No guaranteed earnings, customer satisfaction or virality | Transparent objectives, service recovery, fair lab participation and measured outcomes |

### H5. Operational manuals and system-generated outputs

Maintain versioned, searchable quick starts and task manuals for customer admin, merchant, partner/reseller, developer/builder, finance, staff/support, security/recovery, executive/auditor, student, instructor and lab supervisor. Each manual specifies prerequisite role, task, fields, steps, expected result, exception route, screenshots/demo from the current release and last review. Include account recovery, domain renewal, updating content, approving work, paying/reading invoices, exporting data and seeking help.

The system should generate daily diagnostics; weekly delivery/service/growth reviews; monthly commercial/customer-success/finance reports; and quarterly recovery, access, vendor, policy and product reviews. Each report has period, metric definitions, source freshness, missing-data status, owner and actions. Expose financial, customer, academic and staff information only to the authorised audience. Reports and notifications are designed scope here, not scheduled jobs already installed.

### H6. Reusable next-run instruction

Use the included DUDOS_Master_Execution_Prompt_v2.1.md for future MASTER_BLUEPRINT_UPDATE, CUSTOMER_DRAFT, DISCOVERY_RECONCILE, IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC, STAGING_BUILD, RELEASE_REVIEW and OPERATE runs. Always load the approved parent baseline, this candidate/approved successor as appropriate, the complete lifecycle pack, workbook, country/sector profile, source manifest and versioned templates. Include the lifecycle, commerce/education/partner applicability, source coverage, missing inputs, architecture/API contracts, costs, agent policies, recovery, acceptance and operating controls in the output itself.

The immediate handover is concrete: this integrated master, the expanded workbook, retained v1.1 templates, the execution prompt, machine-readable configuration/agent/automation contracts and source manifest. The next delivery step is Phase 0 current-state verification and a scoped pilot implementation through the existing DUDOS/DAIOS governance route. The package does not send offers, buy subscriptions, deploy sites, charge customers or approve a new constitutional baseline.

[W27 — Google Search Essentials](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials)

Search readiness is not a ranking or indexing guarantee.

[W28 — Google site moves](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)

Map URLs, redirects, indexing and migration checks.

[W29 — Google Drive authorization](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/api-specific-auth)

Select minimal scopes and verify app requirements before customer connection.

[W30 — Stripe webhook guidance](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks)

Verify signatures, handle duplicate/out-of-order events and reconcile state.

[W31 — YouTube API overview](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/getting-started)

OAuth, quota and project compliance constrain publishing.

[W32 — TikTok Content Posting](https://developers.tiktok.com/products/content-posting-api)

App review and platform-authorized posting controls apply.

[W33 — OpenTelemetry signals](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/)

Use linked traces, metrics and logs for diagnosis.

[W34 — WhatsApp announced service-message pricing change](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/non-template-messages)

Official search announces 1 October 2026 change; treat as price-review trigger, not a fixed free-service assumption.

## Appendix 4. Adoption and pilot handover

| Required decision | Owner / record to complete |
| --- | --- |
| Source/authority and controlled baseline | Chairman or delegated governance authority; selected versions, hash, change case and effective date. |
| Current-system reuse and architecture | Technical/security owners; runtime inventory, unresolved historical findings, ADR and contracts. |
| Country, commerce and legal pack | Legal/privacy, finance and merchant/institution owners; applicability, terms and provider eligibility. |
| Pricing and service commitments | Commercial/finance/service owners; pricebook, cost assumptions, support cover and tested recovery tier. |
| Academy and Living Lab | Institution and lab supervisors; curriculum authority, learner safeguards, work/commission terms and restricted pilot. |
| Pilot scope and delivery capacity | Product/delivery owners; named primary/backup team, estimated backlog, dependencies and acceptance dates. |
| Production GO | Authorised customer/provider release authorities; same-version tests, evidence, rollback and operating readiness. |

Approval record: approver and delegated authority ____________________; decision ____________________; exact document/version/hash ____________________; effective date ____________________; conditions and rollout scope ____________________.

## V2-I. Template recovery, governance decisions and activation

### I1. The retrieval gap is closed

All 17 canonical template bodies previously marked unavailable have now been located, retrieved and checked. The earlier warning described the retrieval result of the v2.0 review; it did not establish that the templates did not exist. The v2.1 package includes the existing files unchanged in Recovered_Canonical_Templates_17, with their exact identities, versions and SHA-256 hashes. No replacement bodies were invented.

Each recovered v1.0.0 file contains 13 numbered sections, a controlled input block, a copy-ready execution prompt, domain coverage, deliverables, registers, acceptance gates, routing and change rules. The files identify themselves as Review Candidate - Not Yet Frozen. Availability is now resolved; approval of the individual template versions remains a separate decision. The review verifies structure, common controls, domain scope and routing, and does not certify legal correctness, specialist fitness or production effectiveness.

The revised source manifest contains 112 source records: the previous 95 plus these 17. All 71 canonical routes now have retrieved body references in this package's source register. Fifty-four routes retain their previous source references; the 17 recovered bodies are included locally. Selecting a route still requires the full relevant body, current applicability and the appropriate approval evidence.

| Recovered template | DUDOS use | Responsible review role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MPT-AUD-001Audit, Assessment, Gap Analysis & Assurance | Core assuranceV2-F; V2-H | Independent assurance owner |
| MPT-DOC-001Documents, Reports, Proposals & Communications | Core proposals/contentV2-D; V2-E | Knowledge/commercial owner |
| MPT-LCH-001Launch, Go-Live & Hypercare | For each production launchV2-F; V2-H | Release/service owner |
| MPT-MVP-001Discovery, PoC, Prototype & MVP | Core pilot planningV2-C; V2-H | Product/engineering owner |
| MPT-OFF-001RoleOS, PositionOS & Office Operating System | Core staff accountabilityV2-D; V2-F | Operations/HR owner |
| MPT-OPM-001Operating Model, Process, Workflow & Service Management | Core operationsV2-D; V2-F | Delivery/service owner |
| MPT-PPT-001Presentations & Decision Decks | When decision deck selectedV2-E | Communications owner |
| MPT-STR-001Strategy, Transformation & Roadmap | Core planningV2-A; V2-H | Product/strategy owner |
| MPT-XLS-001Spreadsheets, Models, Registers & Dashboards | Core registers/modelsV2-D; V2-H | Data/finance model owner |

### I2. Include the complete templates in the system

Register each body by template ID, version, source identity, file hash, effective scope, owner and approval record. Keep retrieval state, review state, approved-baseline state and runtime-activation state in separate fields. A source file's candidate label and an approval to use the 71-entry index cannot be converted into a body-level approval automatically.

The workbook now has 71 worksheets. Sheets 00–67 retain the v2.0 structure, with targeted source/routing/decision updates. Sheet 68 Template Closure tracks the 17 bodies and review evidence. Sheet 69 Activation Plan holds 18 owned implementation work packages. Sheet 70 Recovered Inputs contains all 544 source-template input rows. These rows are separate from the existing 573 starter entity fields and 52 customer-profile keys.

The source templates reuse local field IDs such as 001-001. Store a composite key such as MPT-STR-001@1.0.0/001-001, together with customer/project and response version. Never use the local number alone as the database key. The recovered-template catalogue also retains lifecycle steps, domain controls, all 12 deliverables, eight register schemas, ten acceptance gates and companion routes for every recovered body. Keep these source IDs separate from the 16 DUDOS gates.

Use applicability routing to assemble a customer pack: universal governance and the selected general templates first, followed by the relevant sector templates. Health, investment, regulatory and academic templates activate only for applicable customer scope and qualified domain review. DUDOS should reference the verified SIS/LMS, HR, clinical, financial or regulatory system of record where appropriate; including a template does not create a second authoritative backend.

For each selected input, preserve the question, rule, response, source evidence, named owner, review state and version. Draft answers remain editable; missing or conflicting mandatory values produce a precise gap report. Approved outputs pin their source and template versions. Recovered source bodies remain unchanged; material changes go through MPG-LOG-001 and prompt assurance, with an impact map for existing customers.

Green in this integrated blueprint means newly added or revised text. The recovered templates retain their own color legends. The system must read explicit status and approval records rather than infer authority from a color.

### I3. Resolve governance through four concrete decisions

The recommended decisions below are ready for the Chairman or the stated delegated authority to review. They are proposals, with signature, date and evidence fields deliberately unfilled. Current user authorization permits this recovery and drafting work; it does not establish that these governance choices have been adopted.

#### GOV-01 — EEC authority

Retain the verified EADC constitutional authority and UPBIC implementation method. Treat EEC as a subordinate execution/domain layer. Make no authority migration in this release; a later succession requires its own amendment, impact map and approval.

Authority: Chairman / delegated governance authority. Related register: DEC-V2-001; DEC-V2-002. Status: Proposed; decision/evidence to be recorded.

#### GOV-02 — MPIF / MPIP / DAD

Use MPIF = Master Product Initiation Form/data contract, MPIP = Master Product Initiation Prompt/orchestration, and DAD = Development Architecture Declaration. The paired form and prompt share a schema and Initiative ID; retain original source terms and aliases. Qualify problem, owner, buyer, evidence, reuse, risk and boundary through UPBIC G0–G3 before the DAD technology declaration at G4. Register the adopted terms and dependency order in MPG-TOK-001 and MPG-LOG-001.

Authority: Chairman / architecture-governance authority. Related register: DEC-V2-003. Status: Proposed; decision/evidence to be recorded.

#### GOV-03 — DUDOS design and template baseline

Review and adopt the exact DUDOS v2.1 design/specification and selected recovered template versions listed by hash, with conditions and exclusions. Record body-level review and approval in MPG-VER-001 and MPG-IDX-001; index approval alone does not approve the bodies. Preserve all previous versions and customer commitments.

Authority: Chairman / delegated baseline authority. Related register: DEC-V2-001; DEC-V2-004. Status: Proposed; decision/evidence to be recorded.

#### GOV-04 — Pilot delegation and budget

Appoint a primary and backup owner, select one pilot customer/entity/country and service scope, and set a budget and delegated action limits. Permit routine actions only through approved policy and tested controls. Production GO remains specific to release, tenant, domain, enabled capabilities and evidence.

Authority: Sponsor / finance / customer and release authorities. Related register: DEC-V2-006–017. Status: Proposed; decision/evidence to be recorded.

The first recommendation preserves the verified governing baseline and avoids making EEC succession a prerequisite for ordinary DUDOS drafting. An unresolved succession decision affects authority migration. It does not require creating a competing constitution or stopping all useful analysis. Likewise, the MPIF/MPIP terminology decision affects the controlled vocabulary and compiler baseline; original terms can remain traceable while the decision is completed.

Approve scope in layers. A design/specification baseline can be accepted before a production system exists. Template approval establishes permitted controlled use of the specified body. Pilot spending, customer commitments and production activation each follow their own recorded authority. Do not label the whole operating system live because its design baseline has been adopted.

After approval, write the accepted decision into the existing authority/version registers, record the exact object hash and effective date, and create the clean approved baseline required by the source procedure. Preserve this green review edition and all earlier versions. Update only the affected candidate statuses and customer migrations; do not blanket-freeze unrelated templates or sectors.

### I4. Build one working customer lifecycle first

Use a bounded pilot to prove the full chain: completed discovery pack and checklist; validated customer/profile import; template selection; an unissued proposal and price schedule; exact-version approval; staging build; release evidence; controlled activation; billing reconciliation where selected; support; renewals; diagnostics; backup and restoration. The selected pilot should have a real accountable owner, verified scope and measurable customer outcome. Its country, client, budget, providers and dates are not invented here.

Start by inspecting the actual Odoo/Daffodil environment, repositories, installed modules, licences, integrations, data boundaries and operating evidence. Record what can be reused, repaired, configured, integrated or built. Resolve historical findings against the current deployment. The output is an implementation baseline and an estimated backlog, not a new platform chosen only because a tool is fashionable.

| Capability | Implementation route | Configuration record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer / approvals / service | Verify existing Odoo/Daffodil modules and API entitlement | Legal entity; runtime/version; customer/role schema; record rules; API auth; support owner |
| Workflow and delivery | Use existing reliable job engine; assess n8n or equivalent only for a verified gap | Licence/use rights; durable queue; idempotency; retry/dead letters; audit; operator and limits |
| AI and knowledge | Approved API provider behind a bounded model/tool gateway | API project and budget; data terms; region; knowledge permissions; evaluation; logs and kill switch |
| Messaging and channels | Approved email and WhatsApp Business / selected social APIs | Account ownership; opt-in/purpose; templates; scopes/app review; send limits; failure reconciliation |
| Billing and payments | Verified ledger and country-eligible merchant/gateway | Contract; settlement account; tax/currency; sandbox; signature/webhook validation; refund reconciliation |
| Hosting, recovery and export | Existing managed infrastructure with independent recovery controls | Domain ownership; DNS/TLS; backup accounts/keys; retention; immutable copies; measured restore; export destination |

Keep production secrets in a managed vault and reference them by identity. Give every connection a tenant, legal entity, owner, purpose, environment, provider/API version, scopes, contract, quota, budget, expiry and tested failure route. Use official OAuth or provider-issued credentials; do not paste passwords or API keys into discovery forms, workbooks, prompts or support logs.

For AI, connect approved knowledge and a permissions-aware model gateway, then test grounding, cross-tenant denial, malicious instructions in retrieved text, tool limits, spending caps, provider failure and escalation. Staff AI subscriptions and production API access are separate procurement items. Select the provider and plan against the actual workload and current eligibility; the prior candidate list is not a purchase order.

For customer messaging and billing, implement send-time recipient/purpose/version checks, durable jobs, idempotency, retries, a dead-letter queue and provider reconciliation. A queue entry is not delivery evidence; a gateway callback is not settled money until reconciled. If a country or provider lacks an eligible automated payout route, use an approved finance/bank process and preserve the reconciliation trail.

### I5. Acceptance evidence determines activation

The 18 work packages in sheet 69 identify dependencies, accountable roles, required outputs and acceptance evidence. Fill primary/backup names, estimated hours, due dates and actual evidence after inspecting the environment and team capacity. Sequence them by dependency: governance, foundation, staging, verification, release, operation and expansion. These are planning stages, not replacements for EADC, UPBIC or DUDOS gate IDs.

The pilot must demonstrate secure intake and correct template versions; an unpriced draft when prices are absent; approval invalidation after material changes; tenant and revoked-access denial; no duplicate financial or message effect after retries; current country/channel eligibility; independent restoration with measured recovery objectives; controlled cutover/rollback; and successful support, renewal, diagnostic and escalation handling. Use synthetic or authorised test data until the approved production boundary permits live data.

Evidence must identify the tested code/configuration/template/provider versions, environment, test inputs, actual result, timestamp, tester, independent verifier where required, and defect or approval record. Screenshot-only or narrative-only evidence is insufficient where a transaction, permission or restore result can be independently checked. Keep unresolved critical failures visible and stop only the affected release or capability.

Production GO must name the customer/tenant, legal entity, release, domain, enabled capabilities, authorised operator, approved window, recovery plan and evidence package. The deployment process rechecks authority and the same-version evidence at execution time. A signed form for an earlier build does not authorise a changed release. Customer payments, advertising spend, banking changes and student live-work scope retain their specific limits.

For system-led operation, approve routine policy once and let tested workflows operate within that delegation: reminders, ownership routing, backup/export jobs, diagnostics, eligible renewals and permitted communications. Changes outside the limits, expired authority, policy conflicts and failures create an owned exception. Revoke or pause affected queued actions when the relevant approval or policy changes. Keep the human owner accountable for outcomes while the system performs the repeatable work.

During a restricted live pilot, confirm the agreed stability period, daily diagnostic delivery, support responsiveness, customer feedback and cost-to-serve before expansion. Diagnose from observable evidence and retain closure tests. Finance, merchant, academic, health and regulatory authorities keep their applicable decisions; AI does not grant its own approval or override a failed mandatory control.

### I6. Decision and handover form

Decision package: DUDOS v2.1 integrated master and the selected recovered v1.0.0 template hashes in DUDOS_Source_and_Template_Manifest_v2.1.json. Use the package manifest for exact artifact hashes. Record the selected body list and review evidence; do not sign a filename alone.

Approver name and role: ________________________________

Authority/delegation reference: _________________________

GOV-01 decision and conditions: _________________________

GOV-02 decision and conditions: _________________________

GOV-03 selected master/template versions and scope: ______

GOV-04 pilot owner, backup, entity/country, budget and limits: _________________________________________________

Review evidence and accepted exceptions: ________________

Effective date; exact hashes; signature/verified approval record: _________________________________________________

Production GO record, when its evidence exists: __________

### I7. Next execution command

Run DUDOS IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC using the v2.1 integrated master, the completed 71-sheet workbook, recovered-template catalogue, source manifest and the recorded governance decisions. Preserve all 71 canonical routes and source identities. Select templates by customer/country/sector applicability and include their complete inputs, deliverables, register schemas and gates. Inspect the actual environment and reuse evidence, then complete the 18 activation work packages with named owners, dependencies, estimates, acceptance criteria and required provider configuration. Produce the staging implementation backlog and precise outstanding decisions. Carry forward existing applicable authority; do not repeat resolved approvals or infer production authority from document completion.

Record operational capability as Designed, Configured, Tested, Approved for stated scope, Active or Suspended, with evidence and timestamps for each transition. Report template availability separately: the earlier list is now 17 recovered and zero unavailable. Report template adoption, customer readiness and live-system capability independently.

title: Master Website Prompt v3.1 Yellow
body:
<!-- DOCX is authoritative for yellow highlighting and page layout. -->

# DUDOS Master Website Prompt

Version 3.1 Yellow Review Candidate | 15 September 2026

This prompt specifies DUDOS public, customer, staff, partner and administration experiences. It incorporates MPT-WEB-001 v1.3.0 Teal of 14 September, including its exact 216 input IDs, 31 output contracts, 28 registers, 24 gates, W13-01–24 controls and WEB-T001–030 tests in the annex. It preserves predecessor lineage. Neither the source template nor this prompt is an approved production release.

Copy and execute from this point

Act as the DUDOS product strategist, information architect, UX/UI lead, full-stack delivery lead, content editor, accessibility specialist, integration architect, growth analyst and security reviewer. Build the requested website scope or produce the requested design artifacts in the declared mode. Start from the DUDOS master, selected customer sources and existing repository. Complete authorized work and report actual capability evidence.

W01 Run inputs and mode

Yellow v3.1 addition: the final yellow annex supplies the explicit full-source runner, DUDOS-specific bindings, all ten companion routes and the DOL profile requirements. Read it together with the complete inherited source; this standalone prompt does not replace source bodies.

Record mode, organization, tenant/entity, country, languages, domain, product owner, technical owner, commercial owner, customer success owner, selected packages, source versions, assets/rights, current system, required integrations, data sensitivity, target outcomes, timeframe and applicable action authority. Use ANALYSE_DESIGN_PRODUCE for specifications and STAGING_BUILD for authorized implementation. A future publish action must use the current request and recorded scope, not an inferred permission from this document.

Use English and Bangla as the initial DUDOS content languages, with configurable locale, currency, timezone and translation. Other languages and RTL remain configurable by customer scope. Never invent a customer testimonial, staff identity, certification, partner approval, product readiness, price or customer result.

Read and disposition every source input and required deliverable. The annex is an execution contract: inherited requirements are retained; unanswered customer-specific values remain Unknown. Each applicable field must map to a form, table, API, report or explicit non-UI purpose. An N/A decision needs rationale; a deferral needs owner, dependency and date. Surface orphans.

W02 Public proposition and sitemap

The homepage should explain in plain business terms that DUDOS connects a customer's website, commerce and operations, with AI assistance and continuing service. Use a clear assessment CTA, a secondary explore-solutions path and direct login/support links. Organize content around customer outcomes. Describe evidence-backed maturity on detail pages without making every page an engineering document.

| Route group | Required purpose and key content |
| --- | --- |
| /en and /bn | DUDOS proposition, outcome paths, verified proof and assessment CTA |
| /solutions | Website modernization, ecommerce, integrations, AI support, business operations and analytics |
| /industries | Conditional sector packages, relevant workflows and implementation assumptions |
| /packages | Comparable entitlements, setup/recurring/usage distinctions and quote request |
| /transform | Guided existing-site/business assessment with save/resume |
| /integrations | Searchable provider/module catalog with supported/configurable/adapter/manual/unavailable states |
| /marketplace | Verified add-ons, compatibility, rights, support and commercial terms |
| /partners | Partner categories, application, verification criteria and recognition rules |
| /resources and /academy | Guides, learning paths, supervised labs and approved content |
| /newsroom | Verified news, sources, corrections, localized content and newsletter preferences |
| /case-studies | Permissioned evidence, scope, baseline, observed outcome and date |
| /trust | Security/privacy practices, subprocessors as applicable, accessibility and disclosure routes |
| /support and /status | Service help, ticket entry, incident status and verified escalation |
| /legal | Terms, privacy, cookies, acceptable use and country-specific notices |
| /login | Verified identity, organization membership, recovery and appropriate SSO |

Use equivalent localized routes for essential journeys. Domain/path strategy follows the selected deployment rather than blindly duplicating this illustrative route pattern. Search indexes only approved public content. The public chatbot has only public approved knowledge.

W03 Transformation wizard

Step 1 asks what outcome the customer wants and whether a site/system exists. Step 2 captures sector, country, languages, organization scale and current URL. Step 3 inventories ERP/CRM/CMS/commerce/data sources and ownership. Step 4 selects modules, audiences, channels, reporting and expected business results. Step 5 collects brand/content assets and migration quantities. Step 6 requests secure provider authorization where needed. Step 7 presents extracted scope, feasibility, unknowns and proposed package. Step 8 creates a reviewable preview/offer request and next actions.

For every field define stable code, localized label/help, type, validation, required condition, source/owner, default, sensitivity, persistence, permissions, API mapping, retention and test. Required database context such as tenant ID is server-derived; customers must not type their own authority. Dropdowns have stable codes and effective dates; Other creates a taxonomy review item.

Allow draft save, correction and accessible error recovery. Reject unsupported files and show safe feedback. Keep originals, extraction versions and confirmed content separate. No secrets in free text or uploads. URL ingestion has SSRF and untrusted-content controls. Voice transcription remains unconfirmed until reviewed.

W04 Customer and operational workspaces

| Workspace | Core views and permitted work |
| --- | --- |
| Customer | Overview, tasks awaiting customer, requirements, previews, approvals, assets, integration health, packages/usage, invoices, tickets and reports |
| Merchant | Product/stock/order source views, fulfillment, return/refund requests and settlement reconciliation |
| Staff | Assigned work, effort/capacity, blockers, evidence, reviews and handover |
| Partner | Application, verification, listings, assigned opportunities, delivery, support and eligible commission states |
| Finance | Pricebook review, quotes, invoice/provider references, reconciliation, credits and disputes |
| Tenant admin | Organization, verified memberships, roles, brand/locales, integrations and configuration |
| Platform admin | Tenant lifecycle, module releases, service health, bounded support and policy administration |
| Executive and assurance | Jurisdiction-limited outcomes, decisions, certified metrics and evidence drill-down |
| Student and instructor | Selected Academy/Living Lab activities with institutional supervision and safeguards |

Separate organization/group, tenant, legal entity, institution, campus/branch, department, team, position and person. A department is not automatically a separate tenant. One person may have multiple valid memberships. Context switching must isolate drafts, cached data, search, live subscriptions and AI history. Role selectors only choose existing grants; deep links reauthorize at the destination.

Expose distinct feedback, complaint, suggestion and feature-request journeys with status and outcome. Keep private diary/coaching separate from submitted evidence. Prohibit loyalty, political or negative-student profiling and provide confidential reporting, correction and appeal. Apply Master C20 action semantics, WEAR triggers and the KPI Charter gate. Preserve CEPAO/CPO identity uncertainty and PCO coordination distinctions. Privileged authentication follows the development prompt’s MFA and recovery requirements.

W05 Design system and page contracts

Use a clear typography hierarchy, restrained DUDOS branding, readable English/Bangla fonts, strong contrast and generous touch targets. Favor content and task clarity over decorative dashboard density. Provide responsive navigation and coherent components for forms, tables, status, search, filtering, dialogs and notices. Never encode status through color alone.

Each page contract states page ID, purpose, audience, route/locale, source content, visible fields, primary/secondary actions, permissions, data owner, integration, empty/loading/error/denied/stale/success states, analytics events, SEO settings, accessibility checks and acceptance evidence. Show table pagination and export behavior explicitly. Prevent duplicate submission and lost concurrent edits.

Target WCAG 2.2 AA for the selected journeys subject to jurisdictional review. Validate keyboard access, focus, labels, errors, accessible authentication, zoom/reflow, reduced motion, screen-reader announcements and alternatives to charts/media. Confirm Bangla rendering and translations manually. Do not equate automated accessibility scores with conformance.

W06 Administration and controlled editing

Provide a no-code administration studio for pages, navigation, translations, service catalog, approved pictures, forms, custom fields, workflows, reports, notifications, policy parameters and selected organization settings. Distinguish safe configuration from changes requiring engineering. Show exact diffs and a role/tenant/locale/device preview.

Use schema versions, permission dependencies, effective dates, optimistic concurrency, validation, review, release and rollback. Detect destructive field type changes, required-field migrations and broken integrations. AI-generated edits remain visible and reviewable. Deployment does not activate a paid add-on; entitlement and billing transitions are separate.

W07 Business intelligence and dashboards

Each widget states the decision supported, population/scope, source system, period, formula/version, denominator, unit, target, freshness threshold, evidence coverage, drill-down, action and owner. Show missing, stale, partial, disputed and provisional data separately. Provide table/text alternatives.

The customer dashboard emphasizes qualified demand, conversion, orders, settled receipts, service quality, adoption and renewal. Commercial dashboards separate pipeline, recognized revenue, cash and contribution. Staff dashboards show accepted outputs and blockers. Location, hours and commits alone do not establish productivity or misconduct. High-impact corrections need authorized independent review and traceable prior values.

Define consent-aware events for assessment_started, assessment_submitted, preview_ready, quote_requested, quote_issued, contract_accepted, subscription_activated, order_confirmed, payment_reconciled, ticket_opened, ticket_resolved, renewal_completed and export_completed. Implement only events supported by authoritative transitions. Keep public analytics payloads free of private documents, secrets and sensitive staff/student data.

W08 Search content and channel operations

Specify robots/index rules, canonical/hreflang, sitemaps, redirects, structured data, semantic headings, accurate metadata, media rights/alt text and performance budgets. Use crawlable useful pages and original expertise. No special file or markup guarantees AI search appearance. Do not promise first ranking or automatic feed distribution.

The newsroom supports source aggregation, deduplication, editorial selection, weekly/monthly/annual/on-demand editions, translation, approvals, consented distribution, archive and corrections. Official social/YouTube identities need ownership, recovery, verification evidence, permitted embeds/APIs, rights and impersonation handling. Paid media needs advertiser/sector eligibility, claims and destination checks, budgets, consent, rejection handling and appeal.

WhatsApp/email alerts use minimal context and authenticated portal handoff for sensitive details. Distinguish queued, delivered, read, acknowledged, actioned and verified closed. Validate recipients, purpose, opt-in/out, current platform rules, quiet hours and escalation. The in-platform case or notice is the operational record.

W09 AI and MCP surfaces

Keep public, authenticated personal, staff and privileged-admin AI knowledge/tools separate. Distinguish scripted assistance, generative drafts, RAG, recommendations, bounded automation and agentic execution. Numeric autonomy labels are not interchangeable between Student360, SWTechOS, EAACP and Alumni360 AU0–AU5; map allowed actions and risk policy explicitly.

Use cited authorized knowledge, abstention, retention/deletion, prompt/model versions, evaluations, budget, escalation and kill controls. MCP contracts identify client/server/gateway, protocol/transport, issuer/resource/audience, schema/version, purpose, side effects, delegation and expiry. A browser navigation tool is not proof of a production MCP server. Re-review changed tool manifests and prevent token passthrough.

W10 Developer handover and acceptance

Deliver the actual editable repository/source archive when built, with dependency lockfiles, licensed assets, setup/editing guides, environment variable names without secrets, field/route maps, API contracts, real schema/migrations/seeds, tests, deployment/rollback and manifest hashes. Classify storage as physical database, scaffold, browser memory, local storage, external API or proposed schema. Do not invent a database export.

Retain source custody, NDA/IP and licensed use. Replicate using sanitized templates, excluding another customer's people, brands, private policies, credentials and executive grants. Release documentation and training must support staff succession and nonexpert content updates.

Execute all applicable G-WEB gates and WEB-T scenarios in the annex at the declared maturity level. Map each DUDOS extension to baseline requirements, fields, routes, services and tests. Report critical orphans, skipped tests and unavailable sources. A page render or successful build proves only that result. Finish with actual artifacts, observed behavior, remaining decisions and the next bounded action.

Exact inherited template contract

The following annex preserves the retrieved MPT-WEB-001 v1.3.0 input labels and IDs, required outputs, registers, gates, W13 controls, acceptance scenarios and field-contract text. All are retained for applicability assessment. Blank source placeholders are not approved answers. The exact machine-readable source is unchanged. A separate DUDOS applicability overlay supplies the same IDs and per-record dispositions, owners and mapped artifacts. The complete readable source body is also retained in the package because its operating and routing rules extend beyond the extracted rows.

Annex A All 216 controlled inputs

| Source ID | Input and type | Allowed values and requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WEB-001 | Target initiative / website / domain Text | Required; canonical project and product name |
| WEB-002 | Requested action Select | Create / Review / Update / Consolidate / Build / Export handover / Assure / Freeze; action authority is separately recorded |
| WEB-003 | Purpose and measurable outcome Text + KPI | Required; business, user and social outcome |
| WEB-004 | Delivery stage and target date Select + date | Discover / Design / Build / Validate / Launch / Operate / Improve / Retire |

Annex E All 24 W13 requirements

W13-01

Organization hierarchy and customer boundaries. Separate customer account/group, tenant security boundary, legal entity, institution, campus/branch, department, team, position and person. Define stable IDs, parent relationships, memberships, effective dates, status, policy inheritance and allowed aggregation. A department is not automatically a tenant. Each independent customer has a distinct boundary; group executives see only explicitly granted entities and fields. Use configurable owner/deputy roles instead of hard-coding names, brands or Daffodil authority into other customers.

W13-02

Login and active organization context. Specify invitation, self-registration, admin provisioning, federation discovery, verification, sign-in, step-up, account linking, recovery, suspension and sign-out. Record the exact visible fields and server-derived context in Appendix C. Prove membership independently of a claimed email domain. Role choosers only select already granted roles. Every destination independently authorizes a deep link or SSO handoff; a successful sign-in at one product is not permission in another. Where a shared enterprise IdP is selected, use separately registered application clients and protected sessions; do not share passwords, app secrets or unscoped tokens across products.

W13-03

Membership sessions and delegated access. Support a person with several valid memberships or roles through an explicit active context. On switching, invalidate or separate caches, pending drafts, search results, websocket subscriptions and AI context. Define joiner/mover/leaver rules, group changes, delegated authority, substitutes, temporary expert/support engagements, access reviews and expiry. Revoke sessions, refresh grants and queued privileged actions under a specified policy. Account recovery must not become a weaker administrator access path. Deny protected access at effective expiry or revocation, including already-open sessions and downstream resources. Record enforceable downstream revocation bounds; open work or connector failure cannot renew rights. Unsupported enforcement is a blocked dependency or requires an explicitly approved compensating design.

W13-04

Page fields forms tables and actions. Every field and action must have a stable contract, not merely a label on a mock-up. Generate a Field and Form Dictionary covering type, validation, ownership, conditional visibility, privacy, permissions, persistence, API mapping, translation, retention, audit and tests. Bind every applicable field to a screen, table, report, API or explicit non-UI purpose. Map filter/sort/export/bulk-edit behavior to the same authorization rules. Identify required database fields separately from optional visible form inputs.

W13-05

Complete journeys and state transitions. Define every transition by source/target state, trigger, actor, guard, required evidence, approval, side effect, timeout, escalation, retry and terminal condition. Distinguish suggestion, issued direction, approval, execution, verification, certification and publication. Prevent duplicate submission and lost concurrent edits. Include cancelled, rejected, blocked, expired, corrected and reopened states when meaningful. Do not mark a case solved because a message was generated or a task submitted. Bind approval to the exact target, action, record/evidence version, conditions and expiry; changed evidence requires a recorded disposition. Child-task closure must not silently close its parent.

W13-06

Dashboard evidence and decision contracts. Each widget specifies the decision it supports, cohort/scope, source, period, formula/version, denominator, unit, target, freshness limit, evidence coverage, drill-down, permitted action and accountable owner. Show missing, stale, partial, disputed and provisional data distinctly from zero or poor performance. Use a table/text alternative for charts. Compare only role-appropriate measures. Separate workflow coverage, eligible automation rate, total automation share and observed net benefit; targets are not achieved results. Preserve certified/published metric snapshots with immutable version, source lineage and linked restatements. Hours, commits or online presence alone do not establish productivity or integrity; pipeline, recognized revenue and cash remain distinct. Forecasts disclose horizon, assumptions, uncertainty and validation.

W13-07

Shared ownership across products. Create one versioned integration contract shared by affected products and referenced by all prompts. For each domain/field identify the authoritative writer, steward, approved commands, event publisher, consumers and certification/publication owner. A common dashboard or SaaS front end does not transfer ownership of HR, identity, academic, financial or repository records. Prevent uncontrolled duplicate masters and duplicate entry. Reconcile competing contract IDs and versions before write-back.

W13-08

Reliable API and event exchange. Use versioned API/schema contracts with validated tenant, actor and resource context; source record/version; effective and occurrence timestamps; classification; correlation/causation; and idempotency metadata. Specify signatures, audience checks, ordering, replay windows, retries, dead-letter ownership, corrections, retractions, deletions and reconciliation. Use an outbox/inbox or equivalent consistency mechanism where justified. A received envelope is untrusted input until the destination validates scope and authority. Failed or stale sync remains visible. Preserve canonical and native IDs. Distinguish Supported, Configurable, Adapter Required, Manual Only and Unavailable provider capabilities. Reconcile complete pagination and unknown timeout outcomes; a correlation ID is not automatically an idempotency key and transport is not guaranteed exactly once. Carry source health, as-of time and affected scope into dashboards, exports, caches and AI answers. Suppress dependent scoring or actions when required evidence is missing or stale. Restore current status only after reconciliation and revalidation, not a successful connectivity check.

W13-09

Field ownership and safe corrections. Enforce object, row and field permissions in services, storage, search, analytics, downloads, notifications and AI retrieval. UI masks alone provide no data security. Where scores or high-impact records exist, retain formula/policy versions and historical evidence; route corrections through an authorized independent reviewer with a reason, linked prior value, effective date and subject notification. Human decisions are separate records. Do not permit hidden score inflation or silent retrospective formula changes.

W13-10

Accountable work and restricted digital operations. For delivery-oriented products, record one accountable owner, executor, reviewer, deputy, deadline, dependencies, evidence, acceptance and escalation. Link approved directives and meeting decisions to work, repository issue/commit/review, release and measurable outcomes where applicable. Separate read, draft, issue, approve, execute, verify and close. Define protected production/data/access changes, temporary expert access and revocation. Virtual CTO or equivalent AI may advise and prepare work within granted authority; it cannot self-approve.

W13-11

Student employee and vulnerable user overlays. Activate domain-specific personas and fields only when applicable. Student services may include applicant, enrolled student, alumni, guardian/proxy, adviser, faculty, registrar, employer, mentor and scholarship/service reviewer; HR may include employee, recruiter, manager, L&D, Finance, HR and independent appeal roles. Verify relationship scope, purpose and expiry. Preserve private Diary/coaching versus deliberately submitted evidence. Do not create negative-student, loyalty or inferred political-risk scoring. Sensitive cases require proportionate, confidential evidence and human review. Distinguish support, suggestion, survey, complaint, protected disclosure, safeguarding and emergency routes. Define identified/confidential/pseudonymous/anonymous modes, anti-retaliation, small-group disclosure limits and verified relationship sharing. Do not use AI to re-identify anonymous feedback. Emergency routes must have an actual designated contact and immediate non-AI path.

W13-12

Controlled location and security event handling. When field verification is required, define authorized roles, working-purpose/time boundaries, necessary precision, retention, access, offline exceptions and alternative verification. Do not infer misconduct from missing GPS, a failed request or a single metric. Qualify unauthorized manipulation separately from ordinary errors. Warning or lockout rules require defined triggers, evidence, proportionality, recovery and independent review; a three-strike policy is a configurable organizational rule, not a universal default.

W13-13

Admin studios and configurable fields. Provide authorized editing for pages, translations, navigation, forms, custom fields, workflows, reports, policies, catalogs and organization settings. Define which changes are configuration and which need engineering. Version schemas, validations and permission dependencies; detect destructive type changes, required-field migrations and broken downstream mappings. Preview the exact role/tenant/locale/device experience. Use optimistic concurrency or equivalent conflict detection, scheduled effective dates, approval, audit and reversible release. AI-generated edits remain visible diffs. Canonical dropdown/reference data includes stable code, localized label, description, parent, source/owner, effective dates and status. An Other value requires a reason and taxonomy review rather than creating an uncontrolled duplicate category.

W13-14

Updates upgrades add-ons and entitlement. Distinguish code/content/configuration release, security patch, feature upgrade, connector version, database migration and commercial add-on activation. Provide a release center with compatibility, changed permissions, dependencies, entitlement, billing impact, sandbox results, staged rollout, opt-in where required, rollback/forward repair and EOL. Deploying code does not activate or bill an unpurchased module. Renew grants when an extension adds scopes. Keep customer customizations in validated configuration with an explicit inheritance/override model.

W13-15

Separated AI audiences and bounded tools. Keep public, authenticated personal, staff and privileged-admin knowledge and tool scopes distinct. Separate scripted assistance, generative AI, RAG, recommendation, bounded automation and agentic execution in the capability register. Define approved use, retrieved-source permissions, deletion propagation, citations/abstention, memory scope, human escalation, model/prompt versions, evaluation, budgets and kill controls. W13-16

MCP identity and protocol boundaries. Distinguish browser navigation tools, MCP client, MCP server, gateway and downstream API; a locally registered navigation function is not a production remote service. Record protocol version, transport, issuer/resource/audience, client identity, tool schema/version, purpose, read/write/destructive effects, user delegation and expiry. Use separate properly scoped upstream authorization, not token passthrough. Tool-description or manifest changes trigger review; annotations and provider branding are not authorization. Evaluate injection, confused deputy, replay, SSRF and exfiltration.

W13-17

Authoritative notices and human escalation. Use the in-platform task/case/notice record as the operational source. Link a memo to its actual directive or meeting ID and approved issuer when applicable; do not invent meeting references. Distinguish queued, delivered, read, acknowledged, actioned and verified closed. Define channel preferences, deduplication, quiet hours, acknowledgement/escalation rules and backups. WhatsApp/email alerts use minimal context and authenticated portal handoff for sensitive details. Resolve support through an accountable role and deputy rather than one indispensable person.

W13-18

Implementation status and honest public claims. Maintain independent requirement, implementation, verification and approval states. Distinguish Planned, Prototype, Simulated, Reported Built, Verified Pilot, Verified Production and Retired. Every public availability claim names feature, release/environment, supported scope, test/evidence, owner, verifier/date and expiry. A button, source claim, published preview or SSR test does not prove a database, login, API, AI service or production tenant isolation. Label synthetic data and disconnected services. Withdraw stale claims or qualify them.

W13-19

Real data architecture and portability. For each object identify its authoritative system, schema, migration, validation, seed/demo fixtures, live data source, attachments, indexes, retention, backup and export. Classify physical database, empty scaffold, browser memory, device-local storage, external API and proposed future schema explicitly. Separate operational records from AI/vector indexes and analytics projections; propagate correction/deletion appropriately. Do not invent a database dump when none exists. Offline mutation requires an authorized sync/conflict policy and must not cache sensitive data by default.

W13-20

Technology and global deployment decisions. Select technology against current source constraints, team capability, support lifecycle, security, accessibility, hosting/residency, cost, performance and portability through the DAD. Preserve working repositories and lockfiles; do not replace stacks merely to match a template. Distinguish public discovery, authenticated application and administration requirements. Record locale, currency, tax, timezone, language, low-bandwidth, assistive-technology and sector overlays. Re-open current official standards before fixing implementation versions; global readiness is not a certification claim.

W13-21

Release and developer handover. Deliver actual editable source, configuration, dependency manifests/lockfiles, assets, Markdown architecture/setup/editing guides, field/route maps, API contracts, schema/migrations, synthetic seeds, license/SBOM records, test evidence and version/commit provenance. Include a manifest with paths, purposes, classifications and checksums, plus a reproducible source ZIP and available history. List environment-variable names and setup requirements without secrets. Classify original source, generated output, actual database export and proposed material separately; record exclusions and access limitations. Preserve applicable NDA, IP ownership, source custody and licensed-use conditions in the authorized handover; sharing access is a separate action. Freeze accepted release manifests/hashes rather than relying only on mutable links.

W13-22

Pilot rollout continuity and replication. Define the pilot entity/cohort, workflow inventory, data baseline, owners/deputies, training, acceptance evidence, rollout gates, hypercare, reconciliation and recovery. Measure coverage and automation separately and verify benefits. Replicate through sanitized templates and configuration; never copy another customer’s people, confidential policies, credentials, brand or executive grants. Maintain staff succession, support continuity and a readable nonexpert update guide. Every accepted release refreshes its documentation and downloadable handover package.

W13-23

Source coverage and reusable omission detection. Auto-populate inputs from authorized sources with citations and confidence, then disposition every inherited/new input, persona, surface, field, integration, output and gate as Applicable, N/A with rationale, Deferred with dependency/date, or Unknown with an owner. Keep requirement, field, route, data and test orphans visible. Preserve stable IDs during merges; reconcile product module/pillar counts through a crosswalk rather than silently deleting, duplicating or renumbering requirements. A percentage is never a substitute for resolving critical omissions.

W13-24

Execution completeness and evidence scoped approval. Record the requested mode and existing authority once, complete all authorized unblocked outputs, and ask consolidated questions only for unresolved decisions. For long tasks maintain a deliverable manifest and resumable progress; do not label unfinished output complete. Test the declared implementation level: design review, synthetic prototype, connected pilot or production. A passed render/build proves only that check. Prompt approval, architectural approval, production release, commercial availability and public publication are distinct decisions.
