#### PS-008 Create multi-tenant and multilingual market packs

Inputs: tenant_profile_ref; locales; default_locale; markets

Instructions: 1. Design customer/tenant/entity/brand/branch relationships and isolation for the selected organization; verify membership server-side. Shared platform support, analytics and model context do not automatically receive cross-customer data.2. Use stable language-neutral codes, translation-group IDs, locale-specific labels/routes, approved terminology, localized dates/numbers/timezones and explicit fallback. The source language and translated variants share fact provenance but have independent quality/publication review. An updated fact invalidates dependent translations.3. For each target market produce a readiness pack: local audience/service fit, language/RTL testing, currency/tax/payment assumptions, residency/processor/retention decisions, support hours, accessible content and licensed partners. These are requested decisions, not invented legal conclusions or proof of global availability.4. Return tenant/field access rules and cross-tenant/cache/search/export/AI tests, plus locale parity and market readiness. Add other languages through a versioned registry with human QA; selecting a locale alone does not certify translations.

Acceptance: Tenant denial is enforced in API, retrieval, cache and export; Draft translations and unsupported markets remain labeled.

Prior recipe outputs required: PS-004; PS-006.

Output schema: urn:dudos:prompt-studio:ps-008:output:1.0.0. Required keys: recipe_id; recipe_version; run_id; selection_id; actual_mode; environment; capability_status; tenant_context_ref; source_evidence; source_record_dispositions; payload; artifacts; issues; test_results; authority_decision_ref; next_action. Complete nested validation remains in this exact recipe catalogue record.

#### PS-009 Generate API, MCP and connector adoption packs

Inputs: integration_refs; modules; existing_system

Instructions: 1. Resolve each selected integration to a publisher, exact product/version, official documentation, license/commercial rights, tenant-bound connection and source-of-record owner. Classify verified, sandbox, proposed adapter, manual or unavailable honestly.2. Draft versioned API/event/MCP input and output schemas, scopes, issuer/audience/resource, tenant binding, rate/quota/timeouts, side effects, idempotency/concurrency, error handling, callback authenticity, replay protection and reconciliation. MCP is a scoped adapter over governed APIs, not an authorization bypass.3. Use only allowed provider destinations and vault references. Check actual service field mappings and rights before any write. DOL 41 proposed MCP entries still require input/output schemas and live bindings; do not claim this recipe completed them merely by rendering a catalog.4. Return a contract completion matrix, mocked/sandbox test fixtures, mapping gaps, connector version/deprecation records and failure/recovery plan. An unavailable connector may yield a reviewable adapter proposal; it cannot silently send data elsewhere.

Acceptance: No tool activates without typed contract and verified scope; Unexpected outcome requires reconciliation before retry.

Prior recipe outputs required: PS-006.

Output schema: urn:dudos:prompt-studio:ps-009:output:1.0.0. Required keys: recipe_id; recipe_version; run_id; selection_id; actual_mode; environment; capability_status; tenant_context_ref; source_evidence; source_record_dispositions; payload; artifacts; issues; test_results; authority_decision_ref; next_action. Complete nested validation remains in this exact recipe catalogue record.

#### PS-010 Generate an agentic workflow and evaluation pack

Inputs: modules; budget; data_use_purpose

Instructions: 1. Choose bounded agent responsibilities from retained DUDOS AG-01–22 and DOL A01–A20 specializations, preserving both namespaces and source tier meanings. Map purpose to tools, evidence, owner/deputy and deterministic business workflow; role numbering grants no authority.2. Create resumable run/step/checkpoint, lease, handoff, action-intent/receipt and reconciliation contracts by reusing the v3.1 agent runtime schemas. Pass minimized evidence references; receiving agents reauthorize them. Enforce budgets, deadlines, cancellation, rate limits and escalation.3. Separate read/draft/recommend from policy-authorized reversible actions and consequential action preparation. A1-style drafting may continue with sources; finance, identity, publication and provisioning execute only under applicable authority and verified prerequisites. Agents cannot self-approve a new permission.4. Specify evaluations for groundedness, abstention, injection, tenant/field isolation, stale evidence, revoked grants, duplicate effects, cost, latency and business benefit. Current provider/model compatibility and deprecations require official-source verification. Return observed results only if actually tested.

Acceptance: Agent output cannot elevate access or approve itself; Evaluation records separate specification from observed runtime evidence.

Prior recipe outputs required: PS-009.

Output schema: urn:dudos:prompt-studio:ps-010:output:1.0.0. Required keys: recipe_id; recipe_version; run_id; selection_id; actual_mode; environment; capability_status; tenant_context_ref; source_evidence; source_record_dispositions; payload; artifacts; issues; test_results; authority_decision_ref; next_action. Complete nested validation remains in this exact recipe catalogue record.

#### PS-011 Specify commerce, packages, billing and revenue controls

Inputs: modules; markets; service_expectation_refs; budget

Instructions: 1. Model selected goods/services/subscriptions, sourcing role (own, group, resale, white-label, referral), SKU/entitlement, setup/recurring/usage charges, quota, trial, renewal, delivery and support boundaries. Preserve actual provider and seller ownership; never infer resale rights.2. Read approved pricebook/currency/tax/merchant/settlement policy. Where absent, return an unpriced offer structure and finance decisions. Draft estimates are not invoices or available stock/capacity. Document price version, validity, discounts, cancellation and refund authority.3. Specify order/payment/provisioning/fulfilment/return lifecycles and reconcile invoice, provider result, settlement and ledger. Use hosted/tokenized payments where approved and avoid raw card data. Protect callbacks, replay, duplicate order and unknown outcome paths.4. Return package comparison, billing/entitlement state contracts, unit-economics assumptions, reconciliation cases and sandbox tests. Payment collection and service activation remain separate from a generated storefront or quote.

Acceptance: No unsupported price, payment success or available capacity is asserted; Revenue, payment and settlement remain separately evidenced.

Prior recipe outputs required: PS-006; PS-009.

Output schema: urn:dudos:prompt-studio:ps-011:output:1.0.0. Required keys: recipe_id; recipe_version; run_id; selection_id; actual_mode; environment; capability_status; tenant_context_ref; source_evidence; source_record_dispositions; payload; artifacts; issues; test_results; authority_decision_ref; next_action. Complete nested validation remains in this exact recipe catalogue record.

#### PS-012 Specify installation, support and accountable operations

Inputs: modules; service_expectation_refs; reporting

Instructions: 1. Connect accepted scope to installation/provisioning, staff work orders, schedules, materials, customer acceptance, support cases, incidents, renewals and offboarding. Every case has owner/deputy, clock, state, evidence, escalation and closure rule.2. For DOL facilities verify provider/site/resource, institutional reserve, maintenance, eligibility, price/rights and capacity before making expiring atomic holds; do not equate POP proximity with feasibility. Staff work/travel/wait/location evidence follows authorized job and duty window, with correction and customer-refusal paths.3. Define service limits, ticket priority, notification preferences, authorized recipients, handover, monitoring, restoration and source-of-record corrections. Do not copy restricted HR/location/financial detail into public or marketing reports.4. Produce operational runbooks and a report catalog distinguishing missing data from zero performance. Test failed provisioning, partial delivery, duplicate tasks, unreachable customer, disputed acceptance and restore evidence. Cadence configuration is not proof that scheduled automation exists.

Acceptance: Case closure requires verified outcome, not a clicked complete button; Facility, staff and support commitments remain evidence-bound.

Prior recipe outputs required: PS-006.

Output schema: urn:dudos:prompt-studio:ps-012:output:1.0.0. Required keys: recipe_id; recipe_version; run_id; selection_id; actual_mode; environment; capability_status; tenant_context_ref; source_evidence; source_record_dispositions; payload; artifacts; issues; test_results; authority_decision_ref; next_action. Complete nested validation remains in this exact recipe catalogue record.

#### PS-013 Generate competition, student-project and research programme prompts

Inputs: modules; audiences; markets; data_use_purpose

Instructions: 1. Translate a verified industry/customer problem into challenge scope, eligibility, outcomes, sponsor, mentor, resources, selection rubric, timeline assumptions and acceptance. Connect Student360/Alumni360/faculty/partner references only through permitted contracts and consent/purpose rules.2. Separate learning submissions, assessed research, competition awards, customer acceptance and commercial products. Map student teams, external national/global talent, mentors and reviewers by demonstrated capability and fair criteria; conflicts and appeals need independent handling. AI may assist matching or rubric checks, never silently grant awards or fabricate skills.3. Specify IP/background-IP/license, sponsor terms, confidentiality, ethics/data permission, permitted AI assistance, plagiarism/provenance review, credits, accessible participation and remuneration/commission where selected. Restricted datasets and operational systems stay inaccessible until valid grants exist; use synthetic sandboxes for early work.4. Produce programme forms, judging/milestone workflows, resource reservation requirements, evidence-based portfolio and a commercialization handoff. ICC industry–academia pattern is a reference process, not authority to enroll ICC members or copy their research.

Acceptance: Student/competition status does not imply employee, member or vendor authority; IP, ethics, conflict and acceptance records precede restricted access or commercialization.

Prior recipe outputs required: PS-006.

Output schema: urn:dudos:prompt-studio:ps-013:output:1.0.0. Required keys: recipe_id; recipe_version; run_id; selection_id; actual_mode; environment; capability_status; tenant_context_ref; source_evidence; source_record_dispositions; payload; artifacts; issues; test_results; authority_decision_ref; next_action. Complete nested validation remains in this exact recipe catalogue record.

#### PS-014 Generate competition and technology-opportunity analysis

Inputs: markets; modules; channels; budget

Instructions: 1. Define the concrete comparison question, target segment, geography, competitor/service alternatives, time window and decision owner. Retrieve only authorized internal facts and permissible public sources; respect access boundaries and do not fabricate competitor prices or market share.2. Build a dated evidence table comparing functions, positioning, customer fit, pricing basis, operating cost, integrations, security evidence, portability and support. Distinguish advertised claim, independent observation and internal hypothesis. Missing evidence lowers confidence rather than becoming a negative fact.3. Score build/integrate/partner/white-label opportunities using explicit weights, assumptions and sensitivity. Include local and global distribution, language/support readiness, talent/research commercialization, total cost and ecosystem fit. No ranking establishes objective global leadership.4. Produce an experiment backlog and monthly review proposal with source freshness, adoption prerequisites, expected measurable benefit, owner, pilot cost, kill criteria and rollback. Installing a newly discovered tool or changing providers requires an explicit scoped change; a watchlist is not an automatically deployed upgrade.

Acceptance: Every competitive claim records source/date and uncertainty; Technology suggestions create reviewable pilots, not live updates.

Prior recipe outputs required: PS-002.

Output schema: urn:dudos:prompt-studio:ps-014:output:1.0.0. Required keys: recipe_id; recipe_version; run_id; selection_id; actual_mode; environment; capability_status; tenant_context_ref; source_evidence; source_record_dispositions; payload; artifacts; issues; test_results; authority_decision_ref; next_action. Complete nested validation remains in this exact recipe catalogue record.

#### PS-015 Generate or implement the selected solution and migration

Inputs: requested_mode; existing_system; output_formats; approval_refs

Instructions: 1. Resolve all selected recipe outputs, governing full template bodies, source versions and implementation dependencies. In DRAFT deliver code-ready specifications; in PREVIEW deliver an isolated labeled preview; in STAGING_BUILD implement only the authorized slice in the actual repository/environment. Respect existing user changes and project conventions.2. Build one full vertical journey: select scope, ingest evidence, normalize, confirm, compile recipe bundle, generate preview, capture corrections, assign approved build, test, prepare release and support handoff. Wire real adapters only when authorized and available; otherwise implement explicitly labeled synthetic fixtures and disconnected states.3. Create migrations/backfill/redirects with source-to-target reconciliation, dry run, concurrency and database recovery. Suspected compromised runtimes are quarantined; extract reviewed content through a clean path. Record commit/artifact versions, actual auth/database/API/AI modes and build/test evidence.4. Return source artifacts, setup/build/run instructions, environment variable names only, dependency/license inventory, migration plans and known gaps. Do not publish production from source generation or copy an ICC historical deployment configuration into a new tenant.

Acceptance: Actual files and observed checks substantiate implementation claims; Preview, sandbox connection and production remain distinct.

Prior recipe outputs required: PS-003; PS-005; PS-006.

Output schema: urn:dudos:prompt-studio:ps-015:output:1.0.0. Required keys: recipe_id; recipe_version; run_id; selection_id; actual_mode; environment; capability_status; tenant_context_ref; source_evidence; source_record_dispositions; payload; artifacts; issues; test_results; authority_decision_ref; next_action. Complete nested validation remains in this exact recipe catalogue record.

#### PS-016 Generate release review, handover and continuing-update prompts

Inputs: requested_mode; approval_refs; reporting; output_formats

Instructions: 1. Reconcile the exact selected artifact manifest against requirements, MPT 353 dispositions, DOL field/service/agent contracts and all selected recipe outputs. Record missing/unexecuted tests without inventing pass evidence. Accept a release-review plan early when implementation is not yet available; mark execution dependency.2. Assess requirements, source/rights, identity/tenant, security, accessibility, finance, integration, performance, operations, recovery, localization and exit gates according to scope. Historical ICC seven P0s become targeted rechecks where relevant; they do not label a new tenant defective.3. Create separate scoped decisions for document adoption, architecture/data contract freeze, staging entry and exact production release. Existing authorized actions proceed; unresolved gates hold their affected action. A source hash, yellow highlight or signed design does not establish runtime acceptance.4. Return a portable handover manifest, owner/deputy/edit map, tests, source versions, approvals, rollback/forward repair and review cadence. Draft post-launch measurement and monthly improvement prompts with actual evidence and change control. Production execution requires valid authority rechecked at execution time.

Acceptance: Formal adoption and actual release decisions use exact versions and evidence; No unrun test or unknown production outcome is reported as passed.

Prior recipe outputs required: PS-015.

Output schema: urn:dudos:prompt-studio:ps-016:output:1.0.0. Required keys: recipe_id; recipe_version; run_id; selection_id; actual_mode; environment; capability_status; tenant_context_ref; source_evidence; source_record_dispositions; payload; artifacts; issues; test_results; authority_decision_ref; next_action. Complete nested validation remains in this exact recipe catalogue record.

### Selection dependency and conflict rules

PS-R001 Authorize independently. Resolve tenant_profile_ref, source access, grants, entitlements and environment from trusted server records. Reject client-injected roles, tenant IDs and fabricated approval references. A valid delegated approval need not be requested again. Authorization failure blocks only unauthorized resource/action.

PS-R002 Resolve dependency DAG. Topologically resolve depends_on_recipe_ids. Reuse an earlier output only when version/hash, tenant, source set, requested purpose and acceptance still match. Show proposed prerequisite additions to the user; do not silently enlarge billing or implementation scope. Missing predecessors permit planning with marked gaps; affected build waits.

PS-R003 Conditional selected-module dependencies. PS-015 additionally requires accepted PS-007 for selected search channels, PS-008 for multiple locales/tenants/markets, PS-009 for integrations, PS-010 for AI, PS-011 for commerce/billing, PS-012 for staff/ISP/support, PS-013 for talent/competition/research and PS-014 only when its analysis is in scope. Every selected module has an output or explicit deferred safe state.

PS-R004 Static versus operational behavior. static plus membership/commerce/billing/field_operations/ai_assistant or other authenticated workflows requires a governed backend or explicit architecture change. Never satisfy a live workflow with cosmetic form success. Architecture conflict blocks the affected implementation, not public-page draft.

PS-R005 Publishing and rights. Source rights state pending/not_permitted, unapproved factual content or unknown image rights cannot become public. An isolated preview may use visibly synthetic placeholders where permitted. Publish blocked for affected assets/facts.

PS-R006 Locale semantics. default_locale must be in locales; other_review_required needs extra_choices reason. Currency, country, timezone, language tags and tax/data rules resolve to current versioned registries. Human QA is required before public release of selected languages. Locale draft permitted; unsupported locale launch blocked.

PS-R007 Safe migration. legacy_security_state reported_compromised/unknown cannot justify trusting executable backups. Authorize inspection and isolate suspicious files; separate clean content extraction from code/data migration. Unsafe runtime restoration blocked; reviewed-content reconstruction may continue.

PS-R008 No budget-to-authority inference. A numerical budget, quote, capacity request or selected marketplace SKU does not grant spending, entitlement, stock or facility rights. Deterministic policy limits every step and reconciles actual usage. Out-of-budget step stops; completed artifacts retained.

PS-R009 Source/template completeness. Website aggregate retains all 353 MPT records and ten companion routing triggers. Actual body availability/execution is separately recorded. Never treat template names or scoped recipe completion as full governing contract completion. Affected specialized decision remains open; no source record lost.

PS-R010 Evidence-state coherence. written artifact requires a real path and hash; proposed artifact uses null. pass/fail test requires observed result and evidence. released requires exact production authority plus receipt and verified intended outcome. Reject misleading completion records.

PS-R011 Unique and referential choices. source IDs, recipe IDs, field codes and module codes must be unique. Every reference, dependency, output citation and field binding must resolve inside its authorized/versioned scope. Unknown source values are not coerced to empty/false/zero. Return row-level validation and preserve original evidence.

PS-R012 Edit invalidation and replay. Changing selection, source version, locale, rights, prompt/model/tool version or permissions invalidates affected downstream artifacts and approvals. Keep previous versions and yellow diffs. Deduplicate retry by tenant/run/step/effect key; reconcile unknown side effect. Only impacted branches regenerate; exact-version approvals rechecked.

PS-R013 ICC pattern boundary. CASE-ICC-001 is a process case from three retrieved documents and a historical prototype report. The documented URL was not accessible to this review; no live UI audit or new deployed proof exists. Keep original twelve ICC requirements/seventy Yellow clauses in the case; map only selected relevant patterns to a new tenant. No copied identity, credentials, customer data, licensing or claimed current success.

PS-R014 Select and Run interaction. Save Draft stores choices without running. Review Plan shows resolved recipes/dependencies/cost estimate/data use/gaps. Generate starts authorized document/preview work. Build to Staging and Release are separate contextual actions checked against current authority; never an automatic upgrade. User can save/resume/cancel/export; accessible validation identifies affected fields.

### Talent competition and research surfaces

Provide approved public opportunity and challenge listings with filters for eligible audience, subject, country, remote/on-site access, language, deadlines and participation terms. Distinguish competitions from market-comparison reports. Build private application, project workspace, supervisor review, judging/recusal, appeal, research disclosure, rights review and resource-booking states. Public profiles and showcases are separately consented, moderated projections; another institution or programme does not receive hidden submissions or customer data.

Use stable localized URLs, human-reviewed critical text, language/direction attributes, accessible keyboard controls and low-bandwidth resumable forms. A country selector changes the applicable offer, seller, terms, availability and support profile only after readiness has been verified. It cannot make an unsupported payment provider or licence eligible. Keep ranking and performance claims evidence-based.

### ICC method and source boundaries

Three ICC method references were read for this revision. They support document normalization, source-to-requirement/content mapping, prototype, review, staged delivery and change control. The historical prototype commit and old P0 observations are not a current live-site audit. Begin each customer instance with fresh verified identity, content rights, language, price, approvals and source mapping. Do not present ICC as the actual new pilot customer without its own authorization.

DUDOS_Prompt_Selector_v3.1_Yellow.html is an offline configuration aid included with the package. It creates copyable prompt instructions and selection JSON; it does not connect accounts, send sources to AI, build websites or publish. The production UI must implement the described server workflows and pass the relevant tests.

title: Operations and Customer Lifecycle Guide v3.1 Yellow
body:
<!-- DOCX is authoritative for yellow highlighting and page layout. -->

# DUDOS Operations and Customer Lifecycle Guide

Version 3.1 Yellow Review Candidate | 15 September 2026

This guide converts the master into daily work for the DUDOS team. Use it with the complete retained discovery pack, offer/authorization template, 71-sheet checklist and v3.0 implementation register. It supplies work instructions and reusable prompts. Named people, prices, customers, budgets and service promises must come from verified project records.

1 Establish the operating desk

Yellow v3.1 addition: use the final yellow operating instructions for DOL service admission, staff/field evidence, agent exceptions and the scoped adoption/release desk.

Create one intake queue for customers, internal units and partners. Assign a product owner, technical owner, revenue owner and customer-success owner for each offer, plus primary/backup operators and the required independent reviewers. A single person may hold several pilot responsibilities only where separation-of-duties rules permit. Do not assume students or AI agents provide production duty coverage.

Maintain the customer record, accepted scope, tasks, knowledge, approvals, source evidence and service history in the selected authoritative systems. Personal email or phone conversations may supply evidence but cannot be the only location of a business obligation. Record actual deadlines using the relevant timezone, working days and holiday calendar.

Before work begins, identify the currently adopted master, template bodies, pricebook, service policy and delegated permissions. Existing valid authority supports routine actions without repeated confirmation. If authority is absent, complete the draft and record the specific consequential step that remains blocked.

2 Customer discovery and meeting

Use a fresh customer instance of DUDOS_Unified_Client_Meeting_and_Discovery_Pack_v1.1. Do not copy ICC or another customer's people, price, language, permissions or defects. The first meeting should establish the buyer's problem, present process, expected benefit, decision maker, budget range, timing, existing assets, source-system owners and main risks.

Capture the customer's existing website, systems, software versions, integrations, products/services, audiences, service areas, languages, branding and licensed media. Ask what reports the customer actually uses to make decisions, how often they need them and who may receive them. Separate business expectations from technical suggestions. Record unknowns rather than pressuring a customer to invent answers.

Finish with a read-back of outcomes, included/excluded scope, dependencies, next actions, owner, due date and permissions. A recorded meeting or transcript needs the appropriate consent and retention. The meeting decision is distinct from an accepted offer or production release approval.

Prompt OPS-01: Run DUDOS CUSTOMER_DRAFT for [verified customer]. Read [source list] and create a fresh discovery pack, profile and checklist. Extract every requirement with source/version, distinguish facts from assumptions, propose applicable modules, and return unanswered questions with owner and blocked action. Prepare an unissued offer from verified commercial inputs; where prices are missing, keep it unpriced.

3 Assess website and software feasibility

Inventory URLs, important traffic/landing pages, content, forms, media, plugins, data stores, hosting/DNS/email, source code and ownership. Choose enhance, integrate/headless, rebuild or rescue. A public crawl is limited to public content; authenticated access uses a verified authorization flow. Scan uploads and isolate suspect backups.

For each desired integration, confirm vendor/version, documentation, sandbox, license, supported operations, scopes, data owner, rate limits, event capability, cost and exit. Record Supported, Configurable, Adapter Required, Manual Only or Unavailable. Test the selected capability before quoting an unconditional delivery date. An undocumented database export may require a separate data-mapping work package.

Prompt OPS-02: Assess [website/system] using authorized sources. Produce current-state inventory, route/content/asset map, security and data-quality findings, integration feasibility, reuse ADR, transformation route, migration/redirect plan and effort assumptions. Generate a review preview where possible. Distinguish observed findings, inferred risks and items not tested.

4 Prepare package scope and offer

Retain the source offer families Starter, Professional, Enterprise, White Label, Managed Digital Operations and API/Plugin/Agent Marketplace. The v3.0 capability bundles Presence, Growth, Commerce and Operations can be configured within those families; they are a proposed catalog crosswalk, not a replacement brand or adopted price list.

Every SKU needs customer outcome, included modules, limits, implementation scope, prerequisites, responsible seller/operator, support, SLA, location/country eligibility, recurring/usage charges and maturity. Quotes identify setup, migration, integration, content, training, recurring subscription, AI/API usage, hosting/domain, support, third-party and tax separately. Include exclusions, validity, acceptance and change procedure.

Pricing depends on module selection, API readiness, legacy data format/cleanup, deployment location, backup responsibility, GPU/infrastructure needs and implementation effort, following the Chairman's September pricing direction. Test contribution after discounts, payment cost and service labor. Historical global dollar ranges and ROAS figures remain unverified assumptions.

Prompt OPS-03: Produce the offer/SOW for [customer] from accepted requirements and [pricebook version]. Reconcile quantities and modules, calculate setup and recurring economics, disclose assumptions and exclusions, and identify any missing cost or authority. Return the draft offer, internal cost schedule and approval record separately. Do not issue an invoice or contact the customer from this drafting run.

5 Provision install and migrate

After applicable commercial and technical authority, create a provisioning work packet. Reserve resources only through supported providers with expiry and clear ownership. Domain availability and price must be rechecked immediately before commitment. Keep legal seller, technical operator and source ledger distinct. Daffodil Online is the intended domain/hosting/ISP partner where verified and selected.

Use stages: planned, authorized, reserved, processing, provisioned, tested, accepted, active and failed/recovery. Payment confirmation is not provisioning completion. Paid-but-provision-failed cases require an owner, customer communication and refund/retry path under policy. Preserve DNS and email dependencies and institution-reserved capacity.

Migrations use dry runs, source backups, record reconciliation, redirects, content approval, accessibility, payment/integration checks, rollback and customer acceptance. Credential handover uses a secrets workflow. Record administrator training and restore evidence before service handover.

Prompt OPS-04: Prepare and execute only the authorized [staging/pilot] provisioning steps. Validate scope, ownership, dependencies and selected provider capability; record every command and effect; reconcile imported data; test rollback and restore; produce acceptance evidence and unresolved exceptions. Do not advance to Active from a provider request receipt alone.

6 Work packets and daily accountability

Use one work record with directive/customer case ID, requirement IDs, expected outcome, accountable owner, executor, reviewer, deputy, task category, dependencies, estimated effort, due date, actual work/travel/wait time where relevant, state, blocker, evidence, acceptance and reopening history. Keep a parent's completion independent of a single child task.

Daily review asks: What verified output was accepted? What is still pending? What is blocked and by whom? What decision or help is required? What customer or service risk changed? Time is context for capacity, not a sufficient performance score. Missing CRM entries produce correction and review, not automatic wage withholding.

Prompt OPS-05: Review today's assigned work for [unit/date/timezone]. Reconcile tasks against approved scope and evidence. Report accepted, pending, blocked and overdue items, owner/deputy, next action, customer impact and escalation. Draft work packets for approved next actions and update only fields covered by current authority. Never invent times, evidence or acceptance.

7 Weekly execution and management review

Preserve the weekly submission and approval rhythm from the source plans, but schedule it against the actual work calendar. Team dashboards cover development, AI, commercial progress and Chairman exceptions. Provide a reviewer queue, decision deadline and substitute, with urgent security/service matters following their incident path.

Report accepted delivery against plan; release/test evidence; pipeline movement; issued/accepted offers; invoices versus receipts; adoption; incidents; support; open risks; overdue decisions; reusable assets and documentation freshness. Distinguish internal chargeback and external revenue. Flag stale or incomplete source data before calculating performance.

Prompt OPS-06: Generate the weekly execution review for [period]. Use source-system records and certified metrics. Compare planned and accepted outcomes, identify variance and root cause, propose recovery with owner/date, and prepare the decision queue. Attach evidence links and missing-data status. Keep forecasts separate from actual collections.

8 Customer support and recovery

Intake channels create one authoritative case. Record customer/service, issue, severity, impact, contact preference, time, evidence, contractual coverage and owner/deputy. AI may propose troubleshooting from approved knowledge; offer an immediate human path for emergencies or sensitive matters. Never ask the customer to expose passwords in chat.

Maintain response, investigation, restoration and resolution states separately. A delivered message does not prove resolution. Incident communication identifies verified impact, work underway and next update time without unsupported assurances. Post-incident review records cause, timeline, customer impact, corrective action and tested prevention.

Prompt OPS-07: Diagnose [case] from authorized service records. State verified facts, missing evidence, likely causes and safe next checks. Execute only approved bounded remediation. Escalate consequential changes and keep the customer update as a draft unless sending authority and recipient checks are satisfied. Close only against the case acceptance rule.

9 Billing renewal and customer exit

Reconcile subscriptions, entitlements, usage, invoices, provider events, settlements, refunds and disputes. Separate business state from payment transport. Validate callbacks using provider-prescribed signatures or server-side transaction verification. Deduplicate and handle unknown timeout outcomes before retrying a charge or provisioning action.

Renewal monitoring covers contracts, domains, certificates, hosting, provider subscriptions, API support dates, partner credentials and customer approvals. Each asset needs verified owner, expiry, renewal cost, notice schedule and evidence. A reminder is not a completed renewal. Suspension and exit preserve contractual data access/export and legal retention.

Prompt OPS-08: Reconcile billing and renewals for [entity/period]. Match provider and ledger references, amount/currency, status and dates. Report unexplained differences, eligible actions, impending expiries and owner decisions. Prepare drafts only for unapproved charges/refunds; never silently overwrite posted records. Keep payment, commission accrual and payout states separate.

10 Growth content and business intelligence

Plan content around actual customer problems and verified DUDOS capabilities. Select segments, geography, product/price bands and channels using lawful sources. Define a measurable hypothesis and budget before launching a campaign. Track qualified demand and net business contribution, not only followers or impressions.

Use a content record with source, rights, claim evidence, audience, language, channel, campaign, approval, scheduled time, URL/UTM, publication reference, expiry and correction. Newsletters support consent, preferences, unsubscribe, archive and accessibility. Impersonation/fake-account cases use documented evidence and official reporting routes; do not promise removal or investigate private accounts without authority.

Prompt OPS-09: Prepare [campaign/newsletter] from approved sources and [audience/purpose]. Draft localized content and a measurement plan, verify claims and rights, screen destination/platform requirements, and record needed approvals. Provide social/WhatsApp/email variants and tracking definitions. Publish or send only if this run has applicable account, recipient, purpose and action authority.

Prompt OPS-10: Analyze [period] business performance. Reconcile CRM, commerce, ledger and consented analytics. Show conversion, retention, service issues, margin drivers and opportunity hypotheses with source/date and uncertainty. Use Unknown or Suppressed for unavailable demographics. Recommend a bounded experiment with owner, cost, success criterion and stopping rule.

11 Partner onboarding and reward

Create role-specific applications for vendors, builders, resellers, affiliates, consultants, education partners and infrastructure providers. Ask for legal identity, regions, capabilities, portfolio, IP and resale rights, security/privacy, API/sandbox, support, references, proposed commercial model and required agreements. Store sensitive documents securely with reviewer restrictions.

Track submission, completeness, verification, technical/security/commercial review, decision, contract, onboarding, listing, performance, renewal, suspension, appeal and exit. Recognition identifies issuing authority, criteria, evidence, scope and expiry. Distinguish training completion, commercial approval and technical verification.

Prompt OPS-11: Review partner application [ID] against the selected role/country/product criteria. List verified, missing and conflicting evidence, conduct permitted technical checks, and prepare a reasoned recommendation and clarification request. Do not invent certification, award recognition, change listing status or release a commission without the applicable decision and evidence.

12 Monthly improvement and controlled upgrades

Technology and market intelligence reads an approved source list, selected vendor changelogs, security notices, platform policies and internal customer evidence. Triage critical changes promptly; review strategic improvements monthly. Decide whether to reject, investigate, sandbox, pilot or adopt each candidate.

Score proposed changes using evidence strength, customer impact, urgency, cost, effort, security/privacy, compatibility and reversibility. Scores support discussion, not automatic release. Changes to scopes, billing, data use, schemas or provider obligations require specific review. Preserve accepted customer versions and migration choices.

Prompt OPS-12: Run the monthly DUDOS improvement review for [month]. Compare customer feedback, defects, support, cost, adoption, competitors and official technology/policy changes. Produce a ranked evidence-backed shortlist, experiment plans, affected customers, upgrade/rollback requirements, owners and decision records. Do not deploy a suggested plugin or model automatically.

13 Academy and Living Lab delivery

Use the retained 16-week curriculum and 144-hour structure. Each session has outcomes, prerequisite, lecture, demonstration, supervised lab, independent task, evidence rubric and follow-up. Assign instructor and mentor coverage. Distinguish simulated work from live customer delivery.

Living Lab engagements need institutional and merchant scope, consent, safeguards, IP/NDA, access expiry, customer acceptance and transparent commission rules. Grades cannot depend on earnings. Maintain appeals, accessibility, incident escalation and equivalent simulations. Report course completion separately from recognized accreditation or vendor certification.

Prompt OPS-13: Prepare the Academy session or supervised customer lab for [week/project]. Use the approved curriculum, learner readiness, institution and merchant permissions. Produce lesson, demo, lab steps, assessment rubric, evidence template and support plan. Use synthetic data unless authorized otherwise. Record actual learning evidence without guaranteeing jobs or income.

14 Evidence and release desk

Use the baseline sixteen DUDOS gates, applicable higher gates and web gates without collapsing their namespaces. The release desk checks the selected object/version, evidence completeness, tests, critical risks, permissions, commercial terms, operators, recovery and customer acceptance. Informational progress percentages cannot override a failed mandatory gate.

Prompt OPS-14: Run DUDOS RELEASE_REVIEW for [release/version/hash]. Read applicable gate definitions and actual test/approval evidence. Return Pass/Fail/Blocked/Not run for every applicable criterion, with exact gaps and owner. Recommend GO, CONDITIONAL or NO-GO only for the specified scope. Do not mark it approved or deploy it unless the current authority supports that separate action.

15 Practical KPI definitions

| Metric | Calculation or definition | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accepted delivery rate | Accepted due work packets divided by all applicable due packets | Missing evidence remains unaccepted |
| Time to first value | First accepted customer outcome minus onboarding start | Define outcome by package |
| Qualified lead conversion | Qualified opportunities divided by eligible leads for the same cohort | Preserve source and qualification version |
| Activation rate | Activated contracted tenants divided by eligible contracted tenants | Preview is not activation |
| Net revenue retention | Opening recurring revenue plus expansion minus contraction/churn, divided by opening recurring revenue | Same currency/cohort; exclude new logos |
| Contribution margin | Net revenue minus defined direct service cost, divided by net revenue | No result with missing costs or zero denominator |
| Recovery compliance | Successful scoped restore drills divided by scheduled applicable drills | Requires actual drill evidence |
| Workflow coverage | In-scope cases with owner, state, clock and evidence trail divided by all in-scope cases | Coverage is separate from automation |
| Eligible automation rate | Verified automated eligible cases divided by eligible cases | State exclusions and interventions |
| Reuse rate | Accepted capability scope delivered through verified reused modules divided by accepted capability scope | Use consistent complexity basis |

Targets are set by the accountable owner after baseline measurement. No current DUDOS revenue, margin, uptime, productivity or conversion result is asserted by this guide.

16 Decision and handover record

For each open decision capture ID, question, source, recommended option, alternatives, consequences, authority, owner, due date, chosen option, exact version/hash, conditions, evidence, effective date and affected customers. Priorities are authority/glossary, exact template adoption, runtime reuse, pilot, owners/budget, provider/country eligibility, pricebook and service commitments.

The next team action is to inspect the actual platform and prepare one bounded staging lifecycle using the development prompt. Bring the resulting working demonstration, cost model, test evidence and concrete release decision to the review. This document does not appoint staff, activate scheduled jobs or issue customer communications.

## Yellow DOL service and Agentic AI operating instructions

Yellow marks additions from the two-source recheck and expanded team, talent, research and Prompt Studio review. Earlier wording and colors are retained. These additions define a proposed DUDOS implementation; source-derived data, design proposals, runtime tests and approvals remain separate.

## OPS Y01 Service and sourcing desk

For each selected service, verify seller, operator/provider, own/Group/resale/white-label/referral basis, rights, territory, support, effective offer version and actual costs. Use one record across pages, proposals and AI answers. Missing current rates/capacity produce an enquiry or unpriced draft. Do not copy DOL prices, grants, staff or facility claims into another customer.

## OPS Y02 Feasibility and resource desk

Resolve the prospect location and selected service. Public coverage indicators are preliminary. Obtain engineering feasibility and source capacity. Reserve City/Ashulia rack, power, cooling, compute/storage, network, GPU and redundancy under the selected policy; protect institutional and failover reserves. Recheck expiry and current state before commitment. Route unknown or negative capacity to an owned exception.

## OPS Y03 Installation and customer acceptance

Link accepted scope, provider order, payment reference, work assignment, service tests and independent activation verification. Display payment, order and provisioning separately. Paid-but-failed work requires an owner, reconciliation and authorized retry/refund path. A receipt, message or successful enqueue is not completed installation.

## OPS Y04 Daily staff and field review

Reconcile commitments, work/travel/waiting time, accepted output, visits, customer confirmation, materials/expenses, blockers, overdue work and source freshness. Track location only under the approved on-duty purpose and session. Treat denied/low-accuracy/offline data, refusal and disputed evidence as review states. Preserve employee correction and separate executor from verifier.

## OPS Y05 Agent evidence and exception desk

Review attempted runs, verified successes, corrections, escalations, cost, leases/checkpoints and unknown external outcomes. Apply existing valid delegation to routine actions without repeated approval. Pause only the affected action when scope, state, authority, cost or source evidence is missing. Reconcile prior effects before retry. Never certify the agent’s own outcome from its narrative.

## OPS Y06 Weekly improvement and monthly benefit

Use certified or clearly provisional measures to choose a small set of improvements. Record hypothesis, source/date, baseline, owner, cost ceiling, test and stop rule. Report eligible, attempted, completed and source-verified cases separately. Subtract review/exception/maintenance time and all attributable costs from claimed automation benefit. Independently monitor the technology-watch heartbeat and review urgent deprecations on their own deadlines.

## OPS Y07 Academy research and partners

Control interest/waitlist/holds/enrollment/payment, assessment appeals and issuer credentials separately. Research/GPU workloads require dataset rights and quotas. Partner listings need product/territory rights and evidence; commissions depend on eligible settled sales and adjustments. Offer sanitized simulations where live access is unsuitable.

## OPS Y08 Shift handover and escalation

Record owner, deputy, timezone/business calendar, last source update, unresolved issue, next action, deadline, evidence and what is actually blocked. DOL operational reporting uses Asia/Dhaka while events retain UTC. Suggested source response, location-sampling, retention, SLO and recovery values remain proposals until accepted for the actual team and contract.

## Design adoption and implementation release are separate

This revision prepares the evidence for scoped design adoption. The authorized owner may freeze a selected design version with explicit open implementation dependencies; production tests are not prerequisites for freezing every design clause. A formal adoption record must identify the exact version/hash, scope, approving authority, effective date, conditions and migration obligations. No approval has been entered by this revision.

Use four decisions: source reconciliation, design adoption, staging entry and production release. Reconciliation checks establish documentary fidelity and mapping, not approval. Staging with synthetic data can begin under the applicable task authority while provider and operational facts are gathered. A production capability remains blocked by its own unresolved identity, source ownership, rights, commercial, location, security or recovery requirement. Do not block unrelated useful work or close a failed gate through an aggregate score.

Adoption record: selected scope [unfilled]; master and manifest hash [unfilled]; approving authority and evidence [unfilled]; effective date [unfilled]; accepted conditions and exclusions [unfilled]; implementation owner/deputy [unfilled]; customer migration decision [unfilled]. Keep these fields empty until the authorized decision is recorded.

## Yellow operating prompts for the expanded delivery model

### OPS Y09 Source and governance handover

Reconcile exact repository, branch, commit, working-copy changes, source corpus and current interface versions. Separate reported, inspected, tested and live evidence. Route source versions to drafts, sealed decisions to conditional mandates and task evidence to independent acceptance. Preserve routine delegated DUDOS operations and escalate only the affected new/material initiative.

### OPS Y10 Document to website customer desk

Open a fresh tenant/customer discovery record. Capture sources, desired outcomes, rights, language/market, existing URLs and system boundaries. Use the canonical Prompt Studio selection and resolve conflicts. Produce a source-linked preview, reviewed offer inputs, deployment/handover plan and support ownership. Never inherit ICC or DOL identity, prices or grants.

### OPS Y11 Competition and judging desk

Open the selected programme charter and frozen round rubric. Verify eligibility, accessible submission alternatives, conflicts, quorum, evidence, funded prize terms and appeal windows. Summarize with AI only within permitted data scope. Record human award/appeal decisions and keep grades, prizes, work payment and IP rights separate.

### OPS Y12 Student and research delivery desk

Verify supervisor, institution, contributors, source/data/code rights, ethics applicability and reproducibility plan. Assign staged work and equivalent simulations when live access is unsuitable. Review reusable output and commercial rights before product intake. A completed course, research paper or prototype does not certify production readiness.

### OPS Y13 Talent and resource matching desk

Use opted-in profiles, evidence, skills, language, availability, timezone and project constraints. Explain matches, obtain accepted work terms and permit correction or refusal. Confirm lab/GPU/mentor capacity and agreements. Affiliation alone grants no cross-tenant data or resource rights.

### OPS Y14 Country and language launch desk

Review country/entity/offer seller, rights, payment, currency/tax, data flows, critical translations, support, terms and refunds. Record actual evidence and dates. Release only selected ready offers/locales; keep unsupported combinations unavailable and continue independent drafting.

### OPS Y15 Market and technology experiment desk

Review dated lawful competitor and tool evidence, customer feedback and lost deals. Normalize comparable scope, period, geography and currency. Map a proposed improvement to an existing module, owner, hypothesis, cost cap and stop/success rule. Keep the watch inactive until implemented under an actual operating schedule; recommendations cannot amend the canon.

### OPS Y16 Paid pilot and executive evidence desk

Trace source/lead to consent, customer, offer, accepted scope, invoice, settlement, installation, adoption, support and renewal. Separate internal allocation, free reference, billed value, collected cash and realized external revenue. Keep every new work item owned and dated; require accepted evidence for closure. Report missing data and exceptions without masking them with coverage targets.

### Additional scoped implementation decisions

These records supplement the twelve source and field decisions. All are open. The full register records independently permitted work, related requirements and blank approval evidence; no new owner appointment or approval is inferred.

| Decision | Evidence needed | Affected action and owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TEAM-DEC-001 Adopt explicit execution profiles; daily delegated operations do not wait for full DAIOS. | Version-pinned profile and owner-approved routing ADR | Activating the temporary governance adapter without approved authority/migration contractChief Enterprise Architect |
| TEAM-DEC-002 Use separate services/databases first; single-image rewrite remains unapproved alternative. | Repository/runtime/license review and tested interface ADR | Claiming combined implementation or merging codebases based on proseChief Enterprise Architect |
| TEAM-DEC-003 Import as draft; preserve local authorized activation and EADC provenance. | Rule/authority mapping and signed governance procedure | Automatic upstream policy activation inside DAIOSGovernance Integration Lead |
| TEAM-DEC-004 Keep exact four-capability adapter; broader platform capabilities use separate approved contracts. | Contract test for scoped endpoint/capability refusal | Using this key for payment/deployment or any unsupported capabilityDUDOS Runtime Lead |
| TEAM-DEC-005 Allow governed drafting for gate evidence; approve implementation scope before coding/investment. | Existing terminology/order decision resolved with preparation/implementation distinction | Circular requirement that prevents preparing gate artifacts, or coding before scope approvalChief Product Officer |
| TEAM-DEC-006 21 actual domains retained; missing definitions and source twenty-volume / twelve-layer claims remain unverified. | Exact adopted manifest and semantic crosswalk | Certifying full 25-domain / 20-approved-volume / 12-layer coverageEnterprise Architect |
| TEAM-DEC-007 Select one sellable pilot; sequence minimum registries/CRM, payment and support before first-revenue gate. | Named buyer/offer/owner and verified controlled transaction evidence | Claiming Day 90 accepted or first revenue from targets aloneProduct Owner and CRO |
| TEAM-DEC-008 Hard per-record validity preserved; percentages describe adoption backlog only. | Approved metric dictionary with denominator, hard-rule and source evidence | Closing unsupported tasks or admitting ownerless new workQuality and Central MIS Lead |
| TG-DEC-01 Adopt the first programme’s challenge charter, eligibility, rubric, conflicts, quorum, tie/appeal rules and any funded prize terms. | Named programme and responsible institution; Versioned participant/IP/publicity terms; Approved rubric and appeal authority; Prize budget evidence if a prize is promised | Publishing binding participation/prize terms, accepting affected entries under those terms and issuing final awards.Challenge owner and independent judging chair; Finance for funded prizes |
| TG-DEC-02 Resolve ownership, permitted use and commercial benefit-sharing for the selected student/research output. | Actual applicable institutional/funder/employment/student agreements; Contributor and third-party code/data/content rights inventory; Executed license/assignment and revenue-sharing terms for the chosen route; Public disclosure/IP protection decision where relevant | Commercial reuse, redistribution, public disclosure or model training beyond existing granted scope for that output.Rights holders, institution Research/IP office and qualified legal reviewer |
| TG-DEC-03 Approve the actual first live student/talent programme and any cross-institution or resource admission terms. | Named supervisor and maintenance owner; Voluntary participation, work status and applicable compensation terms; Accepted project memberships and data-sharing scope; Programme-specific safeguarding/accommodation route; Actual resource capacity, quota and provider terms where selected | Live participant admission, access to customer data, cross-institution project assets or restricted physical/compute resources.Programme/academic owner, participating tenant and resource owners |
| TG-DEC-04 Select and validate the next country/entity/offer and the languages required for that offer. | Observed demand hypothesis and supported offer; Seller/partner/provider eligibility; Payment, currency, invoice/tax and refund arrangement; Data location/transfer and contractual review for that scope; Real support hours/language capability and reviewed critical localized content | Selling or processing restricted transactions/data for the selected country/offer; this does not prevent viewing a supported language or a lawful lead-only page.Country launch owner with qualified Legal, Finance, data and service owners |

title: Research and Source Reconciliation v3.1 Yellow
body:
<!-- DOCX is authoritative for yellow highlighting and page layout. -->

# DUDOS Research and Source Reconciliation Report

Version 3.1 Yellow | 15 September 2026

The research supports a consolidated commercial platform built on existing Daffodil governance and reusable services. Later Chairman directions resolve the earlier DAIOS/DUDOS hierarchy ambiguity. The main additions are the current web-template contract, a customer transformation configurator, evidence-based commercial controls and a measurable implementation sequence. The complete package preserves original sources and separates proposals from adopted or live capabilities.

Research coverage

Yellow v3.1 addition: the final yellow annex records the targeted two-source recheck and recovered DOL companion. The earlier all-account coverage limits remain unchanged.

Nine attachments were extracted. The primary Drive review listed 360 folders and 2,056 unique file metadata records and retrieved 61 selected bodies. The secondary review fully listed five additional supplied roots and fetched six files plus thirteen selected ecosystem sources. After deduplication, the combined body-source register contains 71 exact Drive file IDs. Retrieved large bodies were analyzed at materially relevant sections; retrieval is not a claim of exhaustive line-by-line verification.

Gmail research used nine searches and retrieved 41 threads containing 523 available plain-text messages dated 19 January to 15 September 2026. The exact DUDOS search was exhausted; three broader searches remain partial. Attachments in email were inventoried rather than independently read, including 14 audio files. Twenty-five official public sources informed the technical recommendations.

The primary inventory retains 1,995 metadata-only files and 99 unlisted descendant folders, including five roots handled by the secondary review. The machine-readable coverage register preserves these identities. There is no claim that every Drive file, historical email, attachment, website or law was audited.

Daffodil Online was resolved through the owner’s Sites catalog as an active version 1 service and operations review workspace. Public page retrieval failed and the returned screenshot could not be downloaded. This verifies the project reference, not its visual quality, runtime integrations or production controls. The failure does not establish that the website is down. Meta Conversions API details and authenticated Meta terms also remain unverified.

Decisions applied in the new package

The current consolidation preserves EADC authority; DAIOS qualification/foundation; DUDOS operations; DDPE commercialization; and DECGS evidence. July hierarchy variants remain historical. EEC succession, MPIF/MPIP/DAD naming/order, exact template adoption and pilot delegation remain recorded decisions. CEPAO/CPO equivalence is unresolved; PCO coordination is distinct.

DUDOS v2.1 recovered all 17 previously unavailable bodies. Their binary hashes were verified locally. Do not repeat the old missing-body warning. The 71-sheet baseline and original 41 worksheet names remain intact, as do 52 profile keys and the separate 544 template-qualified questions.

The website specification inherits MPT-WEB-001 v1.3.0 Teal, dated 14 September: 216 inputs, 31 outputs, 28 registers, 24 gates, 24 W13 clauses and 30 acceptance scenarios. Its complete readable source and exact extracted contract are included, with a separate applicability overlay. Source candidate status remains unchanged.

Legacy DECGS scores have concrete circularity, shifted references, answered-only denominator and approval/calendar problems. Original files remain unchanged. These findings do not establish current runtime defects or permission to sanction staff. Historical prices, revenue samples, staffing, ROAS and speed targets are not adopted commercial facts.

Research synthesis annexes

Attachment analysis and retained control inventory

Read-only analysis dated 15 September 2026. All nine supplied attachments were read. Eight DOCX files were extracted with their paragraphs and tables. All 55 DECGS worksheets and all 71 retained checklist worksheets were parsed. The v2.1 expansions, supporting contracts, source manifest, closure materials and recovered-template catalogue were reviewed. Actual hashes of all 17 recovered DOCX bodies were checked against the catalogue.

The local attachments are snapshots. This subtask does not establish current Google Drive contents, formal adoption, actual staffing, measured commercial results or a deployed runtime. It changed no source files.

Decisions the source evidence supports

DUDOS should be the reusable customer transformation and operating platform: collect goals and authorized assets once; select an applicable package; reuse existing systems through APIs; generate controlled design, proposals, content and builds; deliver with evidence; reconcile billing; support the customer; and improve the service continuously.

Retain the separation of EADC constitutional authority, DAIOS qualification of new initiatives/material changes, DUDOS operations, DDPE commercial distribution and DECGS evidence/intelligence. UADGE is the shared delegated approval engine. The v2.1 EEC succession and MPIF/MPIP/DAD naming decisions remain proposals unless later exact approval is retrieved.

The 72-chapter roadmap, 25-role prompt architecture and 55-sheet DECGS workbook are complementary sources. Their labels and scores do not establish installed capabilities. The new consolidated candidate should preserve their source identities and map duplicate requirements to a single canonical control.

The former 17-template retrieval gap is closed: 17 recovered and zero unavailable from that list. All 17 actual file hashes match the v2.1 catalogue. Availability, individual body approval, design adoption, tested implementation and live activation are different states.

The DECGS workbook contains 27 prefilled operational records with example or unverified historical values. Revenue, approvals, AI accuracy, client status, and gdrive://, crm:// or github:// references must not be presented as current verified facts. Several scoring formulas are defective; they should not authorize development or release.

Source inventory

| Source | Supplied title | Content read | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ATT-01 | Realistic Timeline.docx | 177 paragraphs; 1 tables; 3,934 extracted characters | b32f0363776bdac47454e0c2ce2a5637abb3c7cb542dc03a8a942f343a66dcef |
| ATT-02 | Need to check this prompt latest.docx | 195 paragraphs; 0 tables; 8,301 extracted characters | b38bc45567ae2f0d64c2905c474c10773f6e15650662fd245e1cc2741c2edf7f |
| ATT-03 | Digital operation system guideilines for TEAM.docx | 352 paragraphs; 0 tables; 7,121 extracted characters | 2fe3eb9ad59bccee61ddab9d2237142919e09a2aaed59ecc707102573f9b49ab |
| ATT-04 | Google Drive Mapping.docx | 23 paragraphs; 0 tables; 349 extracted characters | 58ee9e9293d7c2a1e9164b123c29eaf21e6280610b97d4288fce6382f27b2d73 |
| ATT-05 | Weekly Execution.docx | 146 paragraphs; 51 tables; 5,767 extracted characters | 2599f7f478341bce45c565e52aac2c60b4de748b9c739345f22ef8183b0baf7f |
| ATT-06 | DUDOS MASTER PROMPT ARCHITECTURE.docx | 337 paragraphs; 0 tables; 6,114 extracted characters | 2890b01c05af57820afffb7c0fd145132f00162d4371466203a5fae76d39be2e |
| ATT-07 | Strategic Roadmap for Digital Solutions.docx | 1416 paragraphs; 0 tables; 27,973 extracted characters | 1b7cd9e61b7f62e6316d6ecce7d317eff9e47ca065c8b513fa1cfdee8cd896ed |
| ATT-08 | DUDOS_Enterprise_Command_Governance_System_DECGS.xlsx | 55 sheets | 857c91aa0ee58839b7aa6852cac18239309c6386d5cacc31f96dbafff050b033 |
| ATT-09 | Team Structure.docx | 231 paragraphs; 2 tables; 4,316 extracted characters | 559328dd01e9dce167bf63e5112b874407729426bbff5f862f16ccbc901f3d36 |

Exact snapshot IDs, supplied Drive IDs, section text, requirements and workbook schemas are preserved in attachments_requirements.json. These identifiers provide provenance and do not authorize access or source mutation.

Interpretation of each attachment

ATT-01 — Realistic Timeline

The eight phases are:

| Phase | Duration | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foundation | 4–6 weeks | 250–400 hours |
| Knowledge extraction and digitization | 8–12 weeks | 800–1,200 hours |
| Enterprise architecture | 4–8 weeks | 300–500 hours |
| Core platform | 16–24 weeks | 3,000–5,000 hours |
| AI layer | 8–12 weeks | 1,000–1,500 hours |
| Product integration | 16–20 weeks | 2,500–4,000 hours |
| Marketplace and commercialization | 8–12 weeks | 500–1,000 hours |
| Global launch | 12 weeks | Unspecified |

The first seven phases sum to 8,350–13,600 hours. These are historical estimates, not measured capacity or customer commitments. The calendar alternatives are 18–24 months conservative, 12–15 months aggressive and 8–12 months AI-driven. They assume extensive reusable assets, active leadership and dedicated architecture, product and AI capacity. Claimed 70–80% effort savings and 50–70% rework reduction are unsupported estimates.

The role table sums to 13 people, although prose says 12–14 and elsewhere 10–15. Its first 60 days of foundation work is a sequencing recommendation. Preserve the necessary discovery, architecture and approval dependencies without imposing an arbitrary 60-day stop on already-authorized useful work or a bounded prototype.

ATT-02 — Need to check this prompt latest

The opening says, “It may not be correct but we can get it from here.” Treat the document as a proposed enterprise prompt. Fourteen sections address vision, business, connected ecosystems, executive and functional agents, One Person One AI, enterprise data, technology, Odoo 18, CRM/revenue, commerce, dashboards, governance, country expansion and implementation horizons. Its 20 final deliverables include enterprise architecture, SLIP, One Person One AI, roadmap, board presentation structure, technical guide and product backlog.

Preserve the SLIP journey: lead → counseling → admission → enrollment → academic journey → microcredential → internship → placement → employment → alumni → lifelong learning. This is a cross-system journey; Student360, Alumni360, the institutional SIS/LMS, Skill.jobs and HR should retain their relevant authoritative records.

Escrow, wallets, individualized AI memory, health/investment functions and country expansion are proposed capabilities requiring eligibility, purpose, privacy, licensing and authority. DDPE must retain its commercial distribution role rather than replace the DUDOS runtime or EADC authority.

ATT-03 — Digital operation system guidelines for TEAM

Twenty-four clauses establish five pillars: platform, product factory, revenue, governance/trust and innovation ecosystem. Preserve reusable assets, documented design, commercial rationale, AI drafting with accountable review, reuse before build, and system-generated reporting.

The source defines product completion through website, landing page, demo, video, pricing, CRM, sales kit, documentation, knowledge base and support. The four principal product accountabilities are Product Owner for product success, Technical Owner for technical quality, Revenue Owner for the target, and Customer Success Owner for retention and renewal. Retain the additional security, data, knowledge and backup responsibilities from v2.1.

Monthly portfolio review classifies products as Active, Revenue Generating, Needs Attention, Stuck or Retirement Candidate. Products stuck for more than 60 days require escalation. Feedback, complaints, suggestions and feature requests feed the improvement backlog. Preserve asset registers; build/buy/white-label/open-source/SaaS comparisons; country playbooks; central CRM and attribution; weekly dashboards; and faculty/student participation.

The source's “No CRM Entry = No Work Credit” is an evidence-accountability rule. An absent record should trigger correction and review; it does not independently authorize wage denial or adverse employment action. A central commercial engine must still preserve tenant boundaries and separate legal-entity ledgers. Students must not control core architecture or critical production development without qualified supervision.

ATT-04 — Google Drive Mapping

Preserve all 20 numbered folder categories: Governance, Strategy, Business Requirements, SRS, ERD, API, UI/UX, AI Agents, Test Cases, Deployment, User Manuals, Training, Videos, Source Code, Product Roadmaps, Research, Knowledge Base, Prompts, Automation and Archive.

The folder names are a taxonomy, not a complete knowledge system. Every artifact also needs source ID, version/hash, owner and backup, authority, tenant/purpose access, retention, initiative/release links and supersession. The verified repository remains authoritative for source code, with traceable links in the knowledge catalogue.

ATT-05 — Weekly Execution

WEAR contains 16 sections and 51 tables: identification and executive summary; KPIs; deliverables; blockers; approvals; revenue; product factory; AI/automation; cybersecurity; knowledge; customer success; team accountability; risks; lessons; next week; Chairman summary. Every table schema is retained in the extraction.

KPIs cover product and sprint completion, revenue, leads, releases, automation, bug closure, satisfaction, documentation and approval SLA. Every task requires an owner, deadline, KPI, next action and evidence of closure. Completed work needs knowledge capture; released features need approval evidence; revenue opportunities need owners; risks need mitigation.

Approvals pending more than five working days escalate. Blockers remaining for more than two reporting cycles and tasks delayed two consecutive weeks escalate. These rules should create owned corrective action, not artificially close unresolved work. Use business calendars and exact reporting periods. Preserve the daily 15-minute team review, weekly WEAR, monthly executive review, quarterly Chairman strategy review and annual performance/impact report.

ATT-06 — DUDOS Master Prompt Architecture

The document defines one orchestrator and 25 logical agent roles across strategy/governance, architecture/design, engineering/security/operations and commercialization/growth. Retain all 25 catalogue entries and map them to the 22 v2.1 runtime roles by responsibility. A prompt role is not evidence that a runtime agent is deployed.

The 25 roles cover business strategy, Chairman advice, compliance, PMO, enterprise architecture, product engineering, UX, AI architecture, integration, development, DevSecOps, security audit, testing, UADGE, SaaS commercialization, customer success, partners, marketplace, innovation commercialization, investment/exit, portfolio governance, service management, FinOps, training/certification and competitive benchmarking.

Each selected runtime needs sources, permitted tools, owner/backup, scope, prompt/model versions, budget, evidence, escalation and acceptance tests. Preserve the Knowledge Cloud, Chairman Intelligence, enterprise digital twin/scenarios and DUDOS Playbook. Listed technology choices are candidates and must pass the reuse, operating-fit and licence assessment.

ATT-07 — Strategic Roadmap for Digital Solutions

All 72 numbered chapters are extracted as separate requirements. They cover the full ecosystem: business and recurring revenue; infrastructure and deployment; products and marketplace; payments and hosting; partners and APIs; development/security/AI/IP/data; service; internal pilots; sales and student engagement; releases and investment; governance, MDM, identity, credentials and localization; CDP and marketing; knowledge/vendor/FinOps/ESG/recovery/compliance; incubation, intelligence and UADGE; the product factory, digital twin, PMO, lifecycle, Academy and community.

Repeated chapters 52/54 on UADGE, 43/56 on knowledge and 51/53 on DUDOS core should map to single canonical controls while preserving every source reference.

The 36-month strategy uses audit/design in months 0–6, core development 6–12, internal deployment 12–18, commercial launch 18–24 and global scaling 24–36. This is a long-range ecosystem plan and should coexist with a scoped lifecycle pilot. The 99.99% uptime target, 1–3-day customer deployment goals, mobile apps, multicloud and certification lists require capacity, cost, country and acceptance evidence. They are not universal guarantees.

ATT-08 — DECGS

The workbook has 55 sheets and five DECGS layers. It combines older qualification/scoring sheets with 13 operational registers and two executive dashboards. Every operational register intends to require owner, due date, status, revenue impact, approval status, knowledge link, validity, delay and escalation.

Each sheet has 1,000 physical XML rows, mostly empty or formatted. The operational registers contain formula scaffolding through row 204, but only 27 prefilled operational records across those registers. Worksheet row counts are not counts of real customers or transactions.

Preserve original IDs, headers and provenance. Map transactional fields to the selected systems of record, and expose DECGS as an authorized evidence projection. The formula and evidence defects below require correction in a new derivative or implementation; the source workbook remains unchanged.

ATT-09 — Team Structure

Constitutional and operating relationship

July's Master Integrated Edition describes the conceptual chain EADC → DAIOS → DUDOS → DECGS → DDPE:

• EADC: constitutional principles, governance, approval boundaries and controlled change.

• DAIOS: intake, reuse assessment, product initiation, architecture and execution orchestration.

• DUDOS: shared identity, integration, reusable modules, knowledge, AI, infrastructure and revenue capabilities.

• DECGS: strategic objectives, owner/deadline/KPI, approvals, evidence, risk, escalation and executive assurance.

• DDPE: SaaS, marketplace, APIs, AI agents, managed service, white-label, reseller/franchise and external commercialization.

This is a conceptual responsibility chain, not a reason to route every runtime transaction through five services. The new architecture should use bounded services and clear domain ownership. For Daffodil internal deployments, inherit organizational mandates by reference. Independent customer tenants must use configurable authority roles, not the Chairman's enterprise-wide privileges.

The July constitution labels itself “for approval and freeze”; the word Final or Canonical in a title does not provide an approval record. The current DUDOS v2.1 plan makes four proposed decisions: GOV-01 authority/EEC; GOV-02 MPIF/MPIP/DAD terminology and sequence; GOV-03 exact master and body baselines; GOV-04 bounded pilot ownership, budget and delegated actions. Its proposed terminology is MPIF = form/data contract; MPIP = prompt/orchestration; DAD = architecture declaration, with UPBIC G0–G3 qualification before G4 DAD. Earlier sources place DAD before MPIP/MPIF. Preserve aliases and IDs and log the ordering decision rather than silently rewriting history.

The 24 new requirements are: organization/tenant boundaries; login context; memberships/session/delegation; field contracts; state transitions; evidence-backed dashboard metrics; one shared domain contract; reliable API/events; field authorization/corrections; accountable work; student/employee safeguards; proportionate location/security events; admin editing; releases/upgrades/add-ons; separate AI audiences; MCP protocol/identity; notices and human escalation; honest implementation claims; real storage/portability; technology/localization decisions; source handover; pilot replication; source/orphan detection; complete execution with evidence-scoped approval.

Critical design effects:

• A role selector is navigation, not permission. Every destination and every read/export/AI query must independently enforce current membership, object and field grants.

• On tenant/role switch isolate caches, drafts, subscriptions and AI context. Expiry/revocation applies to open sessions and queued actions; a failed connector cannot extend rights.

• Every field needs source, writer, validation, localization, permissions, persistence/API, retention, audit, errors and tests. Every action/state needs actor, guard, evidence, side effects, retries, cancellation and closure evidence.

• A widget must specify decision, source, formula/version, denominator, period, freshness and owner. Missing/stale/disputed is not zero. Pipeline, revenue and cash are separate.

• A shared interface does not make a shared unrestricted database. Signed events retain tenant/actor/source/native IDs, version, occurrence/effective time, classification, correlation/causation and idempotency. Transport is not guaranteed exactly once.

• Admin editing requires exact diff, dependency impact, preview, concurrency protection, approval, effective date and rollback. Schema edits and destructive custom-field changes require migration.

• Code deployment does not activate a paid entitlement or begin billing. Upgrades adding scopes require new grants. Code rollback is not database recovery.

• Public, authenticated personal, staff and privileged-admin AI knowledge/tool scopes stay separate. Numeric autonomy labels conflict between Student360 and SWTechOS; map aliases to explicit allowed actions, never infer permission from A3.

• Web/email/WhatsApp alert delivery, reading, acknowledgement, action and verified closure are distinct states. Sensitive notices use minimal context and authenticated portal handoff.

• Disclose Planned, Prototype, Simulated, Reported Built, Verified Pilot, Verified Production and Retired separately from review/approval. A published preview does not prove real authentication, database, API, AI or tenant isolation.

• Preserve private diary/coaching, confidential complaints, protected disclosures and human appeal. No negative-student, loyalty or inferred political-risk score; no automatic misconduct conclusion from GPS gaps or one metric.

• Provide editable source ZIP, manifest/checksums, locked dependencies, env variable names only, actual schema/migrations/seeds/contracts, license records, source history and actual test evidence when software is built. At design stage provide the handover specification and identify missing implementation files.
